translations.text: To the tune of “This is the confessors.”
This day, my Lord, has gladdened kings, priests, and prophets, for on it their words were fulfilled and all became reality. [Refrain: Glory to you, Son of our Creator. Repeat.]
For today the Virgin gave birth to Emmanuel in Bethlehem. The utterance spoken by Isaiah became reality today.
This one was born there, who counts the peoples in the book. The song that David sang found its fulfillment today.
The word that Micah spoke became reality today: a shepherd came forth from Ephrathah, and his staff shepherded souls.
Look, [?] a star from Jacob, and a leader arose from Israel. The prophecy spoken by Balaam received its interpretation today.
Again, the hidden light descended, and his beauty shone from a body. The dawn spoken of in Zechariah shone today in Bethlehem.
The light of kingship dawned in Ephrathah, the town of kings. The blessing that Jacob pronounced found its fulfillment today.
Again, the tree of life brings hope to mortals. Solomon’s hidden proverb received its interpretation today.
Today a child was born, and his name was called Wonderful. For it is a wonder that God revealed himself [as] an infant.
The Spirit had likened him to a worm, whose birth is without mating. The figure drawn by the Holy Spirit received its meaning today.
He grew up like a root before him, a root from thirsty ground. What was spoken in a hidden way came to pass openly today.
The King was hidden in Judah, and Tamar stole him from his loins. Today the triumph of the Beauty whose hidden presence she loved has shone forth.
Ruth had lain down beside Boaz because she saw the medicine of life hidden in him. Today her vow was fulfilled, for from her offspring dawned the one who gives life to all.
Adam had laid a debt upon the woman who came forth from him. Today she repaid him his debt, for she bore him a Savior.
A man, who never gives birth, gave birth to Eve, the mother. How much more should Eve’s daughter be believed, that she bore a child without a man!
The virgin earth had given birth to that Adam, the head of the earth. Today the Virgin gave birth to Adam, the head of heaven.
Aaron’s staff had sprouted, and dry wood bore fruit. Today its mystery was explained by a virgin womb that gave birth.
Let that people be ashamed, who hold the prophets to be truthful! For if our Savior had not come, their words would have proved false.
Blessed is the True One who came from the Father of truth, fulfilled the words of the truthful, and found his fulfillment in their truth.
From your treasury, my Lord, from the treasures of your Scriptures, let us list the names of the righteous of old who waited to see your coming.
Seth, who took Abel’s place, looked toward the slain Son, through whose slaying the sword that Cain brought into the world would be blunted.
Noah saw the holy sons of God suddenly become wanton, and he waited for the holy Son through whom the sexually immoral were made holy.
The two brothers who covered Noah looked toward God’s Only Son, who would come and cover the nakedness of Adam, who had become drunk with pride.
Shem and Japheth, being merciful, waited for the merciful Son, who would come and free Canaan from slavery to sin.
Melchizedek awaited him; holding his place, he looked forward to seeing the Lord of the priesthood, whose hyssop made creation clean.
Lot saw how the Sodomites had overturned the proper order of nature. He looked forward to the Lord of all natures, who would grant holiness beyond nature.
Aaron awaited him, seeing that if his staff swallowed serpents, his cross would swallow the serpent that had swallowed Adam and Eve.
Moses saw the serpent that was fastened up and healed the bites of venomous snakes. He waited to see the one who would heal the wound inflicted by the first serpent.
Moses saw that he alone had received God's radiance. He awaited the one who would come and, through his teaching, make many godlike.
Caleb the scout carried the cluster of grapes on a pole and came back. He waited to see the grape whose wine would comfort creation.
Joshua son of Nun awaited him, to behold the power of his name. For if he became so great through his name, how much greater would he become through his birth!
That Joshua, who also picked and carried some of the fruit with him, awaited the Tree of Life, to taste its fruit that gives life to all.
Rahab looked forward to him. For if the scarlet thread, as a symbol, saved her from wrath, through that symbol she tasted the reality.
Elijah longed for him, and because he had not seen the Son on earth, he believed and became exceedingly pure, so that he might ascend and see him in heaven.
Moses and Elijah looked forward to him. The humble one rose from the depths, and the zealous one descended from the heights, and they saw the Son between them.
They depicted the mystery of his coming: Moses represented the dead, and Elijah represented the living, who will fly to meet him when he comes.
In return for the death that the dead have tasted, he makes them first. Those who come last, who are not buried, will be caught up to meet him at the end.
Who can enable me to count the righteous who awaited the Son? Their number cannot be fully recounted by our feeble mouths.
Pray for me, my beloved, that I may be strengthened for another occasion. Come, allow me to offer a taste of them in another discourse, as best I can.
Who is able to praise the true Son who has dawned upon us, whom the righteous longed to see in their own generations?
Adam awaited him, for he is the Lord of the cherub and could bring him in and settle him among the branches of the Tree of Life.
Abel longed for him to come in his own days, so that, in place of the lamb he had offered, he might see the Lamb of God.
Eve looked forward to him, for the nakedness of women is great. He could clothe them, instead of leaves, in the glory he had taken off.
The tower that many people built pointed symbolically toward the one who would descend and build on earth a tower that leads up to heaven.
The shelter for the animals also pointed, as a figure, toward our Lord, who would build the holy Church in which souls find shelter.
In the days of Peleg, the earth was divided into seventy languages. He awaited the one who, through languages, would divide the earth among his apostles.
The earth, which the flood had choked, was calling to its Lord in its silence. He descended and opened baptism, and through it people were lifted up to heaven.
Seth, Enosh, and Kenan were called sons of God. They awaited the Son of God, so that through mercy they might become his brothers.
Methuselah lived a little less than a thousand years. He awaited the Son, who grants as an inheritance everlasting life that never ends.
50. Grace herself had asked on their behalf, in a hidden mystery, that their Lord would come in their generations and supply what they lacked.
For the Holy Spirit, who was within them, stirred them on their behalf through silent meditation, and in her they saw the Savior for whom they longed.
The soul of the righteous sensed the Son, who is the medicine of life. They longed for him to come in its days, so that it might taste his sweetness.
It was for him that Enoch longed. Though he had not seen the Son on earth, he believed deeply and was found worthy to ascend and see him in heaven.
Who could deny the grace of that gift which the earlier generations did not receive through great labor, but which came freely to the later generations?
Lamech too looked to him, the Merciful One, to come and comfort him in his toil and the work of his hands, and concerning the earth that the Righteous One had cursed.
Lamech saw that the mysteries of the Son were portrayed in his son Noah. In place of that distant Lord, the nearby symbol comforted him.
Noah too longed to see him, having tasted the help he gave. For if his symbol preserved the animals, how much more would he himself give life to souls!
Noah awaited him, having experienced that through him [?] stood firm. For if his symbol gives life in this way, how much more does he give life in his own person!
Through the Spirit Abraham perceived that the Son’s birth was far off. Instead of seeing him in person, he longed to see at least his day.
Isaac longed to see him, having tasted salvation. For if his sign gives life in this way, how much more does he give life in his reality!
Today the Watchers rejoiced because the Watcher came to awaken us. Who would sleep on this night, when all creation is awake?
Because Adam had brought the sleep of death upon creation through his sins, the Watcher descended to awaken us from the stupor of sin.
Let us not keep vigil like the oppressors, who think about the money they have lent and stay wide awake at night calculating principal and interest.
The thief is awake and alert; he has dug a hole in the ground and buried his sleep. His entire purpose in staying awake is to make those who sleep sweat all the more.
The glutton too stays awake: he has eaten too much and is burning. His wakefulness has become his torment because he did not restrain himself within proper limits.
The merchant too stays awake, wearing out his fingers at night as he calculates how much his capital has yielded and whether his investment has doubled or tripled.
The rich man too stays awake, for wealth has driven away his sleep. His dogs sleep while he guards his treasures against thieves.
The anxious man too stays awake, his sleep swallowed up by worry. His end stands beside his pillows, yet he stays awake worrying about the years to come.
My brothers, Satan teaches one kind of wakefulness in place of another, so that we may be asleep to good things but watchful and awake for evil things.
Judas Iscariot too stayed awake all night, selling the blood of the Righteous One who had purchased all creation.
The son of darkness clothed himself in darkness, having stripped off and thrown away the light. For silver, the thief sold the very Creator of silver.
The Pharisees too, sons of darkness, stayed awake all night. Those dark ones kept vigil to cover the light that cannot be confined.
But you, keep vigil like shining lights on this radiant night. Though its color is black, it is glorious in its power.
For whoever stays awake and prays in the darkness like a victorious champion is clothed in hidden light within that visible darkness. 75.
A hateful person who stands in daylight behaves like a child of darkness. Although he wears light on the outside, he is wrapped in darkness within.
My dear ones, let us not take pleasure in merely being awake, for whoever does not keep watch as he ought keeps a vigil without righteousness.
Whoever does not keep watch purely—his wakefulness is sleep. Whoever does not keep watch cleanly—even his vigil works against him.
The envious person's vigil is a cargo full of loss, and his wakefulness is a trade full of mockery and contempt.
If an angry person keeps vigil, his vigil is disturbed by anger, and his wakefulness becomes full of rage and curses.
If a talkative person keeps vigil, his mouth becomes a thoroughfare: he is eager for idle talk but lazy about prayers.
If a discerning person keeps vigil, he chooses one of two things: either to sleep peacefully or to keep watch righteously.
This is a serene night, in which the Serene One dawned, who came to make us serene. Let nothing enter our vigil that could disturb it.
Let the ear's passage be cleared; let the eye's gaze be modest. Let the heart's thoughts be sanctified; let the mouth's speech be purified.
Today Mary hid within us leaven from the house of Abraham. Let us therefore love the poor as Abraham loved the needy.
Today rennet from the house of merciful David fell among us. Let each person have mercy on his persecutor, as the son of Jesse had mercy on Saul.
Today the sweet salt of the prophets was scattered among the nations. Let us acquire a new flavor through it, for the former people lost their flavor with it.
On this day of salvation, let us speak with discernment. Let us not speak needless words, lest we become needless to him.
This is the night of reconciliation; let no one be angry or gloomy on it. On this night of the One who brings peace to all, let no one be threatening or agitated.
This is the night of the Gentle One; let no one be bitter or harsh on it. On this night of the One who brings peace to all, let no one be threatening or agitated.
On this day of forgiveness, let us not demand payment for wrongdoing. On this day of joys, let us not distribute sorrows.
On this gentle day, let us not be fierce. On this peaceful day, let us not be angry.
On this day, when God came to sinners, let the righteous person not exalt himself in his own mind above the sinner.
On this day, when the Lord of all came to slaves, let masters also stoop lovingly toward their slaves.
On this day, when the Rich One became poor for our sake, let the rich person also share his table with the poor.
On this day a gift came forth for us without our asking for it. Let us, in turn, give alms to those who cry out and ask us.
This is the day that opened heaven's gate to our prayers. Let us also open our doors to petitioners who have sinned and pleaded.
Today the Lord of natures underwent a change beyond his nature. It is no hardship for us also to turn our evil will around.
The body is bound by its nature and cannot grow larger or smaller, but the will has the power to grow to any measure.
Today divinity imprinted itself in humanity, so that humanity too might be adorned with the imprint of divinity.
The end.
Another by Mar Ephrem. To the tune of “The Heavenly Assemblies.”
With the heavenly assembly sent forth to offer praise, at the glorious season appointed for salvation, and on the blessed day reserved for rejoicing, let me join
in love, I too, and rejoice. With gentle melodies I will praise him; with a holy voice I will sing to him. I will glorify that Child who saved us. [Refrain:
Make me worthy, too, to offer you praise with your harp on the day of your birth.]

The harps of the prophets who proclaimed him sang before him. The hyssop of the priests who loved him they also waved before his face, together with the crown of the kings in his lineage, before that Lord
of virgins, whose mother too is a virgin. As King, he gave the kingdom to everyone; as Priest, he gave forgiveness to everyone; as the Lamb, he spread food for everyone.
All the king’s cities are accustomed to offer golden crowns in their hands. The cities of Judah, my Lord, offer crowns endowed with speech;
with their mouths they offer their crowns to you, Jesus: little Bethlehem and Nazareth, Bethany, Shechem, and Samaria, together with the towns that were found worthy and crowned you.
Your city will offer you the first crown: two crowns together, Mary’s and Ephrathah’s. And all the cities together, in their ranks—look, to you
they offer their crowns from what is yours. A king, my Lord, takes without giving. Your cities weave your victories together and offer a crown to your glory.
Let his mother bow before him and offer him a crown, for Solomon’s mother made him king and crowned him. He became an idolater, and his crown was defeated in the contest. Behold the Son of David,
who brought victory to the house of David and crowned it! For you have greatly exalted his throne, greatly raised up his family, and stretched the sound of his harp to every place.
The mother who bore him is worthy of remembrance; the bosom that carried him is worthy of blessings. So too is Joseph, who by grace was called father
to the true Son, whose Father is glorified, the Shepherd of all creatures, who was sent after the sheep that was lost and had gone astray, and carried it back in honor and brought it into his fold.

He has made me happier than all those who were healed, for I conceived him. He has exalted me above everyone who became great through him, for I gave birth to him. I am destined to enter his living paradise,

and in the place where Eve was defeated I will praise him. For out of all the women who were created, he chose me to be his mother, because he so willed; and he became my child, because it pleased him.
Bethlehem will give thanks to you, for she was found worthy of your birth. She will weave Micah’s saying into your crown. Prophecy has become a garden of flowers. She will call the prophets
and kings to help with her crown, for Moses carries symbols of him, and Isaiah joyful mysteries, and lilies [?] in every book.
Through the mouths of my illustrious ones I give thanks that I received him, the infant Son of the Hidden One, when he came out into the open. Let him raise me to the great height among my holy ones,
so that in the vast, spacious heavens I may praise him. They are filled with his glory, yet cannot contain within themselves the greatness of the one who stooped down and became small in a manger.
Heavenly voices proclaimed you to those below; the ears of those above drank you in through the good news: a new spring that the heavenly beings opened for earthly beings
who thirsted for life but had not tasted it. O spring that Adam had not tasted! He opened twelve springs endowed with speech, and they filled the world with life.

Joseph bows before you and offers you a crown—that troubled righteous man whom the angel reassured. So that you might increase his reward, he carried you away in flight in his bosom. The righteousness
of Joseph testified to you, how pure you are. For who could have persuaded the righteous man to carry a despised adulterer’s son and be pursued from one place to another?
You, my Lord, teach me how and why it pleased you to shine upon us from a virgin womb. Was it after the likeness of pure Adam, who was fashioned from earth—
virgin earth that had not yet been tilled? Why, then, was it necessary for the daughter of David to be betrothed to Joseph, and only then for you to be born from her without a man?
The genealogy of kings was recorded under men's names rather than women's. Joseph, son of David, was her betrothed for the Son of David [?], since a child cannot be registered in his mother's name.

Thus he became Joseph's child without his seed, and his mother's child without a husband. Through both of them he linked him to their family, who were recorded among the kings as descendants of David.
It was not fitting for him to be born from Joseph's seed, nor to be conceived by Mary without Joseph. Mary bore him, but he was not registered in her name; and Joseph—

who registered him—he was not his offspring for him to register. Without Joseph's body, his name was attached to him. Without Mary's betrothed, her son shone forth. He became David's Lord and also his father.
Moses called a betrothed woman a man's wife. He also called her betrothed her husband, though he had not married her, so that they would not cut off the genealogy of the Son of David. “Without—

a man,” they say, “how can he be counted as a son of David?” Her betrothed, then, was counted as her husband. Our Lord also acknowledged their lineage: they called him the Son of David, and there was no denial.
If an adopted child is called a man's son, although he is unrelated to his ancestry and family, and because the man desired him he becomes an heir by choice, who—
would doubt the bodily birth of our Savior, who was conceived by that daughter of David, embraced in the arms of a son of David, and worshiped in David's town?
What, indeed, was the chaste woman doing at that time when Gabriel was sent to her, flew down, and descended? Perhaps she saw him while praying at that time, for Daniel too—
saw Gabriel while praying. For prayer and good news, its kinswoman, ought to gladden one another, as Mary gladdened Elizabeth her kinswoman.
The dove carried good news to prayer. At Abram's prayer, his good tidings followed one another. Hezekiah's prayer and his good news came swiftly. The centurion—
his good news gladdened his prayer. Simeon was gladdened with a reward, and Zechariah with the reward of his censer: over his censer his good news came. [19 [?]] All—
good tidings head toward the harbor of supplication. That good news of good tidings, the cause of every joy, found Mary at prayer and [?] her.
Gabriel, like a dignified, composed old man, entered and greeted her so that she would not be alarmed, lest the modest girl see a young man's face and become distressed.
To two chaste elders and a young virgin—to them alone Gabriel was sent with good tidings. They were alike in will, and their natures [?]—
the virgin, the barren woman, and faithful Daniel. One brought forth revelations in words, another a voice for the wilderness, and the virgin the Word of the Most High.
So that he would not bewilder those who saw him by his immensity, he confined himself, from the whole world to the land of the Hebrews, from that whole land to Judah, and from Judah to Bethlehem—
until he filled a little lap. And though he became a seed in our garden and a little ray of light for the pupil of our eye, he shone forth, spread out, and filled the world.

So that his ancestry might be clearly explained—whose son he was—Luke and Matthew traced and listed his family. They reckoned him a son of Abraham, of David, and also of Joseph, so that through the mouths—
the eloquent mouths of two witnesses, and that of the blind man who called him the Son of David, shame might increase for his enemies and the crown might grow greater for those who love him.
Judah's line had never ceased, nor had a ruler from him ever been cut off. From our Lord onward it was brought to an end, because he had fulfilled it.

The long passage of time also bears witness that it has confused the reckoning of generations, and it is no more. The line of descent reached you and stopped, for you are the Son of David, and there is no other.
The first is finished.
Again, to the tune of “He Comforted with Promises.”
Blessed is the child who today has gladdened Bethlehem. Blessed is the infant who today has made humanity young again. Blessed is the fruit who lowered himself to meet our hunger.
Blessed is the Good One who quietly enriched all our poverty and supplied our need. Blessed is he whose compassion brought him down to visit our sickness. Refrain:
Blessed, my Lord, is your birth, which has raised up our lowly condition.
Thanks to the fountain that was sent for our forgiveness. Thanks to him who abolished the Sabbath by fulfilling it. Thanks to him who rebuked leprosy, and it did not
remain. Fever also saw him and departed. Thanks to the Merciful One who bore our distress. Glory to your coming, which brought humanity to life.
Glory to him who came to us through his Firstborn. Glory to the Silent One who spoke through his Voice. Glory to the Exalted One who was seen through his appearing.
Glory to the Spiritual One who willed that his offspring should become a body, in which his power could be touched, and that through that body the bodies of his kin should live.
Glory to the Hidden One whose offspring became visible. Glory to the Living One whose Son became dead. Glory to the Great One whose Son came down and became small.
Glory to the Power who fashioned a form for his greatness and an image for his hiddenness. With both eye and mind we have seen him.
Glory to the Hidden One who cannot be fully grasped, even by the minds of those who investigate him, yet in his grace was touched by human hands.
The nature that had never been touched was bound and shackled by his hands, nailed and crucified by his feet. Of his own will he made himself tangible to those who seized him.

Blessed is he whom free will crucified, because he allowed it. Blessed is he whom even the wood bore, because he permitted it. Blessed is he whom even the tomb enclosed, because he accepted confinement.
Blessed is he whose will brought him to the womb and birth, to the lap and upbringing. Blessed is he whose changes brought our humanity to life.
Blessed is he who sealed our soul, adorned it, and betrothed it to himself. Blessed is he who made our body a dwelling for his hiddenness. Blessed is he who interpreted in our language
his hidden things. Let us give thanks to the Voice whose glory was sung on our harp and whose power on our lyre. The nations gathered and came to hear his melodies.
Glory to the Son of the Good One, whom the children of the Evil One rejected. Glory to the Son of the Just One, whom the children of wickedness crucified. Glory to him who freed us and was bound
in place of us all. Glory to him who stood surety and himself paid the debt. Glory to the Beautiful One who fashioned us in his likenesses. Glory to the Pure One who did not look at our stains.
Glory to him who sowed his light in the darkness and was reproached for its ugliness, though he had covered its hidden parts. He stripped off and took away from us the garment of stains.
Glory to the Most High who mixed his salt into our minds and his leaven into our souls. His body became bread to bring our dead condition to life.
Thanks to the Rich One who paid [?] on behalf of us all what he had not borrowed, and again gave a written pledge and became our debtor. With his yoke he broke off us the bonds of our captor.
Glory to the Judge who was judged, who seated his twelve to judge the tribes, and through unlearned men condemned the scribes of that people.
Glory to him whom we can never measure. Our heart is too small for him, and our understanding is weak. He astonishes our littleness with the richness of his distinctions.
Glory to the all-knowing one who was laid down and asked to hear and learn what he already knew, so that through his questions he might reveal the treasure of his help.
Let us worship the one who enlightened our minds through his teaching and opened a path for his words through our hearing. Let us give thanks to the one who gave his fruit to be tasted
in these [?]. Thanks to the one who sent his heir, so that through him he might draw us to himself and also make us heirs with him. Thanks to that good one, the source of all good things.
Blessed is he who did not rebuke, because he was good. Blessed is he who did not neglect us, because he is also just. Blessed is he who kept silent and rebuked, shining
in both. His silence is powerful and reproves us. His severity is gentle, even when he accuses: he rebuked the deceiver and kissed the thief.
Glory to the hidden cultivator of our thoughts. His seed fell in our soil and enriched our minds. Its harvest came a hundredfold into the storehouse of our souls.
Let us worship the one who sat down and rested, who walked along the road and was himself the Way upon the road, and the gates for those who entered through him into the kingdom.
Blessed is the shepherd who became a lamb to atone for us. Blessed is the vine shoot that became the cup of our salvation. Blessed also is the grape, the fountain of the medicine of life.
Blessed also is the farmer who himself became the wheat that was sown and the sheaf that was harvested. He is the architect who became a tower to shelter us.
Blessed is he who fashioned for himself the senses of our minds, so that with our [?] we might sing what a bird's mouth cannot sing with its melodies.
Glory to the one who saw that we chose to resemble wild animals in our anger and greed, and who lowered himself beneath us so that we might become heavenly.
Glory to the one who has never needed us to thank him, yet is needy because he loves us and thirsty because he cherishes us. He asked us to give to him so that he might give still more
to us. His fruit was mingled with our humanity, so that through it I might be drawn toward the one who bent it down toward us. Through the fruit of the root, he would graft us onto his tree.

Let us give thanks to the one who was struck and gave us life through his wound. Let us give thanks to the one who took away the curse through his pains. Let us give thanks to the one who put death to death by his own death.
Let us give thanks to the one who kept silent and vindicated us. Let us give thanks to the one who cried out against death, which had swallowed us. Blessed is he whose help emptied the left side.
Let us praise the one who stayed awake and put our captor to sleep. Let us praise the one who slept and shook off our stupor. Glory to God, the physician of humanity.
Glory to the one who was baptized and drowned our wickedness in the depths, and strangled the one who strangled us. With every mouth let us praise the Lord of every means of deliverance.
Blessed is the physician who came down and operated without pain, and healed wounds with medicine that was not harsh. His birth became a medicine that shows mercy to sinners.
Blessed is he who dwelt in the womb and built within it a temple in which to dwell, a sanctuary in which to be, a garment in which to shine, and armor with which to conquer.
Blessed is he whom our mouths cannot adequately thank, for his gift is greater than those who speak, and the senses are unable to give thanks
for his grace. For however much we thank him, it is little. Yet because it does no good for us to remain silent and suffer loss, let our weakness offer the song of our thanksgiving.
Good one, who does not demand more than our strength allows, how severely will your servant be judged over the principal and interest, since he did not give what he could and withheld what he owed
! Ocean of praise, who needs nothing, accept in your grace a drop of thanksgiving that my tongue has poured out through your gift, to your praise.
The end.
Another hymn for the season of the Nativity. To the tune of “They Gathered”: “Let Us Celebrate in the Month of Nisan.”
Blessed, my Lord, is that first day of yours, in which this day of your feast was prefigured. Refrain:
Blessed is he who gave you to us when we had not asked for you, so that through you we might thank your Father for his gift.
Your day resembles you, for it loves humanity: it is handed down and comes to every generation.
It is a day that finishes its course with the elderly, then returns to dwell with newborn children.
It is a day that renews itself in its love, so that its strength may renew our old age.
When your day has visited us, passed by, and gone away, it returns in its compassion and visits us again.
It knows that humanity is needy; it resembles you in every way as it asks after humanity.
Creation needs its fountain, and all creation thirsts for it, my Lord, just as it thirsts for you.
It is a day that makes its yoke rule over the ages; time, which conquers everything, does not make it pass away.
For even kings have passed away with their images, and the festivals commemorating them have ceased.
The dominion of your day is like your own: it extends over the generations that have come and those still coming.
Your day resembles you: although it is one, it has branched out and multiplied to become like you.
On this day of yours, my Lord, which is near to us, we have seen your birth, which is far away.
May your day be like you for us, my Lord; may it be a mediator and a guarantor of peace.
Your day reconciled heaven and earth, for on it the Most High descended to those below.
Your day is able to appease the Righteous One, who is angry at our sins.
Look, your day has forgiven our countless debts, for on it mercy dawned upon the guilty.
Your day is great, my Lord; may it not become small through us. May it, as is its custom, have mercy on our foolishness.
If your forgiveness overflows every day, my Lord, how much more may it abound on this day!
All the days have received good things from the treasury of your glorious day.
All the festivals have become beautiful and adorned from the treasures of this festival.
Pour out your mercies upon us on your day, my Lord; make your day known to us above all other days.
For the treasury of the day of your birth is great; may it pay on behalf of those in debt.
This day is greater than other days, for on it the Compassionate One went out to sinners.
Your great day is a storehouse of medicines, for on it the medicine of life dawned for the wounded.
This day is a treasury of benefits: on it, light shone upon our blindness.
Indeed, it comes bearing a sheaf for us, from which abundance flows to satisfy our hunger.
This day is the first cluster of grapes, in which the cup of salvation lay hidden.
This day is the firstborn feast, which takes precedence over and surpasses all festivals.
In winter, which strips the branches of their fruit, fruit dawned for us from a barren vine.
In the frost, which strips all the trees bare, a shoot sprang up for us from the house of Jesse.
In Kanun, when seed is hidden in the earth, an ear of life sprouted from the womb.
In Nisan, when the seed sprouts into the air, the sheaf sowed itself in the earth.
Death harvested it and ate it in Sheol, but the medicine of life hidden within it tore him apart.
For in Nisan, when lambs bleat in the pasture, the Passover Lamb entered the womb.
From the very river from which the fishermen came up, the catcher of all was baptized and came up.
From the river whose fish Simon used to catch came up the one who caught him, the fisher of people.
On the cross, which catches all robbers, he caught that robber for life.
Through his death, the Living One emptied Sheol; he tore it open and sent whole multitudes flying out of it.
The Holy One caught the snares of the crafty one—tax collectors and prostitutes, unclean snares.
The sinful woman who had been a snare for men, he made a mirror for repentant women.
The unproductive fig tree that had withheld its fruit presented Zacchaeus like a fruit.
It had not yielded its natural fruit, but it yielded one fruit endowed with speech.
Our Lord dangled his thirst above the well, and with the water he requested he caught the thirsty woman.
He caught one soul at the spring, and then through her he caught the whole town.
The Holy One caught twelve fishermen, and then through them he caught all creation.
It was Iscariot who escaped from his snares, and a noose fell around his neck.
The net of the one who gives life to all catches people for life, and whoever escapes it escapes from life.
Who can enable me to recount the extraordinary benefits hidden in you, my Lord?
How much can a thirsty mouth express from the fountain of divinity?
Answer the voice of our supplication today; let our prayer in words become deeds.
Make us worthy, my Master, of all that we have seen; may your feast surpass the good things we have heard.
Our mind is distracted among the voices. O Voice of his Father, bring peace to the voices.
The world is in turmoil; let it grow still in you, for in you the sea grew still from its waves.
The demons rejoiced when they heard the voice of blasphemy; let the watchers rejoice in us as they usually do.
From within your flock comes a voice of sorrow. In you, who gladden everyone, let your sheep rejoice.
Do not be disgusted with our clamor, my Master; our mouth thunders, though it is sinful.
May your day, my Lord, bring every joy; with flowers of peace let us celebrate your Passover.
On the day of your ascension, may we be exalted; let its commemoration be held with the new bread.
Our Lord, increase our peace, so that we may celebrate the three feasts of the Godhead.
Your day is great, my Lord; let it not be mocked. Everyone honors the day of your birth.
It is right [?] to honor the day of your birth, for Herod honored the day of his birth.
An impure dance pleased the tyrant; may the voice of chaste women please you, my Lord.
May the voice of chaste women please you, my Lord, so that you may keep their bodies holy.
Herod’s day resembles him; your own day, too, resembles you.
The day of the troubled man was troubled by sin; your serene day is serene like you.
The tyrant’s feast killed the herald; at your feast everyone proclaims praise.
On the murderer’s day, the voice was silenced; but on your own day there are festive voices.
The impure man extinguished the lamp at his feast, so that darkness might conceal the adulterers.
The holy season sets out lamps, so that darkness may flee with its hidden things. / 70 The day of that fox stank like him; holy is the feast of the true Lamb.
The day of the passing man passed like him; your day, like you, endures forever.
The tyrant’s day was dissolute like him, for by his violence he silenced the righteous voice.
The feast of the gentle one is gentle like him, for his sun shines upon his oppressors.
The tyrant knew that he was not king; therefore he made room for the King of kings.
The whole day, my Lord, is not enough for me to weigh your praise against his disgrace.
May your day, O merciful one, overlook my folly, for I weighed your day against an unclean day.
For your day is great beyond comparison, and it cannot be compared with our days.
A human being’s day is that of an earthly being, and God’s day is that of God.
Your day, my Lord, is greater than the prophets’ days, yet I took it and set it alongside a murderer’s day.
You know, my Lord, as the one who knows everything, that you will hear the comparisons my tongue has made.
May your day grant us the request for life, for that man’s day granted the request for death.
On his festival the needy king swore that half his kingdom would be the reward for a dance.
But may your own feast, O you who enrich everyone, pour out [?] in alms.
From thirsty earth a spring gushed forth, sufficient to satisfy the thirst of the nations.
From a virgin womb, as from a rock, a seed sprouted from which harvests came.
Joseph had filled countless storehouses, but they were emptied and exhausted during the years of famine.
A single true ear of grain yielded bread—heavenly bread that never runs out.
The bread that the Firstborn broke in the wilderness ran out and passed away, though it was very abundant.
He returned and broke new bread, which ages and generations cannot exhaust.
They exhausted the seven loaves he broke, and they also finished the five loaves he multiplied.
The one loaf he broke surpassed all creation: the more it is divided, the more it increases.
He also filled jars with abundant wine. They poured it out, and it ran out, though there was much of it.
Though the cup he gave contained only a little to drink, its power is immensely great and inexhaustible.
The cup receives all kinds of wine, but the mystery within it remains the same.
The one loaf he broke has no limit, and the one cup he mixed is inexhaustible.
The grain of wheat that was sown for three days rose and filled the storehouse of life.
It is spiritual bread, like its giver; it gives life spiritually to spiritual beings.
But whoever receives it in a bodily way receives it heedlessly, in a bodily way.
It is the bread of mercy; the mind receives it discerningly, like a medicine of life.
If sacrifices to the dead, in the name of demons, are sacrificed and eaten symbolically…
How fitting it is for us that the mystery of holy communion should be celebrated among us in purity.
Whoever eats from a sacrifice offered in the name of demons becomes demonic, beyond dispute.
Whoever eats the bread of the heavenly one becomes heavenly, beyond doubt.
Wine teaches us that it makes anyone who is [?] by it like itself.
For it greatly hates the one who loves it: it makes him drunk, drives him mad, and mocks him.
Light teaches us that it makes the eye, the daughter of brightness, like itself.
Through the light, the eye saw the nakedness and hurried to cover the modest man.
Wine itself caused that nakedness, for it does not know how to spare even the modest.
The Firstborn put on the crafty one's armor, so that with the weapon that had killed he might in turn give life.
Through the wood with which he killed us, we were delivered; through the wine that drives us mad, we were made chaste.
Through the rib that had been drawn out of Adam, the evil one drew Adam's heart away.
From that rib a hidden power dawned, which cut Satan down as it did Dagon.
For a book was hidden in that ark, crying out and proclaiming the victorious one.
There too was a clear symbol: Dagon was brought low within his own sanctuary.
Fulfillment followed the symbol: the evil one was brought low in the place where he felt secure.
Blessed is the one who came, in whom the symbols of the left and the right were fulfilled.
He fulfilled the mystery represented by the lamb, and he fulfilled the pattern represented by Dagon.
Blessed is the one who saved us through the true Lamb and overthrew the one who overthrew us, as he did Dagon.
In December, when the nights are long, the day that has no end dawned for us.
In winter, when all creation is gloomy, beauty came forth and gladdened all creatures.
In winter, which makes the earth barren, virginity learned to give birth.
In December, which stills the earth's labor pains, virginity experienced labor pains.
No one sees a newborn lamb before the shepherds do.
So too, at the birth of the true Lamb, the news of him hurried to the shepherds.
Perhaps there too the wonder was doubled: a lamb spoke and came forth before its due month.
For a lamb to become, before its time, a herald of that Lamb who conceived him is not natural.
The old wolf saw the suckling lamb and was terrified of him, who was in disguise.
For because the wolf had put on sheep’s clothing, the Shepherd of all became a lamb in the flock.
When the greedy one rushed upon the meek one, the Mighty One tore that devourer apart.
Holiness dwelt bodily in the womb, and now dwells spiritually in the mind.
Mary, who conceived him, shunned marriage. Let the soul in which he dwells not prostitute itself.
When Mary became aware of him, she left her betrothed. Look, he dwells among chaste women, if one is aware of him.
The deaf person does not perceive loud thunder, nor does the brazen person perceive the voice of the commandment.
For the [?] is untroubled when the thunderclap comes, and the brazen person is untroubled by the sound of warning.
Does terrifying thunder rebuke the deaf person? Does terrifying wrath rebuke the unclean person?
For a deaf person not to hear is no fault; but for someone to trample underfoot is insolence.
Thunder occurs from time to time, but the voice of the law thunders every day.
Let us not stop our ears, for the openings that stand open and cannot be closed accuse us.
The gate of hearing is open by nature, so that its compulsory openness may rebuke our insolence.
The will can open and close the gates of the pupils and the gate of the mouth.
That we might see [?] the Good One gave us to hear; [?] that they might be closed [?].
[?] its movements come from our will.
Glory to that Voice who became a body, and to the exalted Word who became flesh.
Ears heard him, eyes saw him, hands also touched him, and the mouth ate him.
Members and senses, give thanks to him who came and gave life to the whole body.
Mary carried a silent infant, while all tongues were hidden in him.
Joseph carried him, and hidden in him was the silent nature that is older than all.
He lay like a little child, and hidden in him was the treasury of wisdom that provides for everyone.
He lay there and suckled Mary’s milk, while all creatures suckled from his goodness.
He is the living breast of living drink. The dead suckled from his life and came to life.
Without a supply of air no one lives; without the Son’s power no one stands.
On his life-giving sustenance, that of the one who gives life to all, depend the souls above and below.
Even while he was nursing on Mary’s milk, he himself was nursing all creation with life.
And while he dwelt in his mother’s bosom, all creatures dwelt in his bosom.
He was silent like a baby, yet he was issuing all his commands to all creatures.
For without the Firstborn no one can approach the divine Being, whom he is able to reach.
During the thirty years that he was on earth, who was governing all creatures?
Who was receiving all the offerings, the praise of those above and those below?
He was wholly in the depths and wholly in the heights; he was wholly with everyone and wholly with each one.
While his body was being formed within her womb, his power was assembling every limb.
While the Son was being formed as a fetus in the womb, he himself was forming babies in the womb.
While the Son was being formed as a fetus in the womb, he himself was forming babies in the womb.
Nor was his power weak on the cross in the same way that his body was weak on the cross.
For when he raised the dead while on the cross, was it his body that raised them, or his will?
Likewise, while he dwelt wholly in the womb, his hidden will was accomplishing everything.
For see: he hung wholly on the cross, yet his power shook all creation.
For he darkened the sun and shook the earth; he split open the tombs and brought out the dead.
Indeed, see how he was wholly on the cross, while also being wholly with everyone.
Likewise, he was wholly in the womb, while also being wholly in everything.
Just as he raised the dead while on the cross, so, while he was a baby, he was forming babies.
While he lay slain, he was opening tombs; while he was in the womb, he opened wombs.
Come, my companions, hear about the hidden Son, who was revealed in his body while his power remained hidden.
For the Son’s power is unrestricted power; the womb did not confine it as it did the body.
For while he, the Power, dwelt in the womb, he himself was forming babies in the womb.
His power embraced the woman who embraced him; for if he withdraws his power, everything falls.
He is indeed the Power that holds all creatures; even while he was within the womb, he did not let go of anything.
He was shaping a form for himself in the womb, while shaping every person in every womb.
While he was growing up in a poor household, he was feeding everyone from his treasury of abundance.
And while she who anointed him was doing so, he was anointing everything with his dew and rain.
The Magi offered myrrh and gold, while the treasure of riches lay hidden in him.
Myrrh and spices, which he had brought into being and created, the Magi offered him from what was his own.
Through the strength that came from him, Mary was able to bear in her womb the one who bears everything.
From the great treasury of all creatures, Mary gave him everything she gave.
She gave him milk from what he had brought into being; she gave him food from what he had created.
As God, he gave milk to Mary; then, as a human being, he suckled it from her.
Her hands carried him because he had lightened his might; her lap embraced him because he had made himself small.
Who could measure the extent of his greatness? He reduced his dimensions to fit a garment.
She wove and clothed the one who had put off his glory; she measured and wove for the one who had made himself small.
The sea bore him, grew calm, and stood amazed. How, then, did Joseph's lap bear him?
Sheol's womb received him and was torn apart. How did Mary's womb endure him?
He split the stones over the graves with his voice. How did Mary's lap endure him?
You came in humility to give life to everyone. Glory to you from all who have received life through you!
Who can speak about the hidden Son, who came down and clothed himself in a body in the womb?
He came forth and suckled milk like an infant; the Son of the Lord of all crawled among little children.
They saw him in the street as a little child, while love for all dwelt in him.
In the open, the Watchers surround him in fear.
Among little children he was cheerful like a child; among the Watchers he was fearsome like a commander.
He was fearsome to John when it came to untying his sandals, but welcoming to sinners who kissed his feet.
The Watchers saw him as Watchers do; each person saw him according to the measure of his knowledge.
In his Father alone is the full measure of knowledge of him, for he knows how great he is.
Yet in varying measures the beings above and those below possess knowledge of him.
He is the Lord of all, who gives us everything; he enriches everyone, yet borrows from everyone.
He gives everything as one who needs nothing, then turns and borrows everything as one in need.
He gave cattle and sheep as their Creator, then turned and asked for sacrifices as one in need.
He made water into wine as its Maker, then turned and drank from it as a poor man.
At the banquet they mixed his drink from what was his own. He mixed his own wine and gave it to drink where he had been invited.
Through his love old Simeon became great: a mortal presented the one who gives life to all.
By the strength that came from him, Simeon carried him. He himself was his offerer, yet he was offered by him.
He had given Moses the laying on of a hand on the mountain, and he received it from John in the river.
Through the power of his gift John was able to do it: the earthly man baptized the heavenly one.
By the strength that came from him, the earth carried him. It was about to dissolve, but his power strengthened it.
Martha fed him from what was his own; she set before him foods that he had created.
All who gave made offerings from what was his own; from his treasury they placed gifts upon his table.
The end.

Teaching Hymns for the Nativity
To the tune of “Who Is Able to Speak?”

This is the month that bears within it every joy: freedom for slaves, pride for the free, garlands for doorways, comfort for bodies. In its love it spreads out even purple garments, as for a king.
Refrain:
Glory to you, beautiful Child of virginity!
This is the month that bears within it every victory. It frees the spirit, subjects the body, brings forth life among mortals, and in its love pours divinity upon humanity.
In this month slaves reclined on beds, free people reclined on rugs, and kings reclined on fine woolen bedding. In a manger the Lord of all lay down for the sake of all.
Look: in Bethlehem King David wore fine linen, but David’s Lord and David’s Son hid his glory in swaddling clothes. He gave his swaddling clothes as a robe of glory to humankind.

On this day our Lord humbly exchanged splendor for dishonor—our Lord humbly exchanged it—because Adam had exchanged truth for wrongdoing. Like a trader, the Good One showed him mercy; his arrangements overcame those of the perverse.
Let everyone drive away their weariness, for that Majesty did not grow weary of being in the womb for nine months for our sake, or of spending thirty years in Sodom among the dissolute.

When the Good One saw that the human race was poor and brought low, he made festivals like treasuries and opened them to the lazy, so that the feast might stir the lazy person to rise and become rich.
Look, the Firstborn has opened his feast to us like his treasury. For only one full day in the year he has opened this treasury. Come, let us be diligent and become rich from it before they close it.

Blessed are the watchful, for they have plundered from it the spoils of life! It is a great disgrace when someone sees his companion carrying treasures out, while he himself sits dozing in the treasury, only to leave empty-handed.

On this feast let everyone adorn the door of his heart; [?] his door, so that the Holy Spirit may enter, dwell there, and sanctify it. For behold, she goes around to every door, seeking where she may dwell.
On this feast the gates rejoice before the gates, and holiness rejoices in the holy temple. A voice thunders from the mouths of children, and Christ rejoices amid his festival like a mighty warrior.

At the Son’s birth, the king had registered people for the poll tax, so that they would owe him. A king came forth for us who erased the bonds of debt and wrote another bond in his own name, so that he himself would owe us.

The sun triumphed and traced a symbol through the steps by which it ascended for twelve days. Behold, from its ascent until today, the thirteenth day, there is a complete symbol of the Son’s birth and of his Twelve.

Moses confined the lamb in Nisan, on the tenth, as a symbol of the Son, who came into the womb and confined himself there. On the tenth he came forth from the womb, in this month when the light triumphed.

Darkness was defeated to proclaim that Satan was defeated, and the light triumphed to cry out in triumph that the Firstborn was victorious. The dark one was defeated along with darkness, and our Light triumphed along with the sun.
Joseph loved the Son and served him as an infant. He rejoiced in him as God and as the Good One, yet was cautious before him as before the Righteous One. What great bewilderment!

Who has granted me, Son of the Most High, that you should be my son? I suspected your mother and wanted to dismiss her. I did not know that within her womb was a great treasure that would suddenly enrich my poverty.
King David arose from my family and put on a crown. I came to great lowliness: instead of being a king, I became a carpenter. Yet a crown has come my way, for in my arms is the Lord of crowns.

Mary overflowed with restrained words and sang to him: Who has granted a deprived woman the power to conceive and bear the One who is manifold, small and also great, who is wholly with me and wholly with everyone?

On the day when Gabriel entered my humble dwelling, he suddenly made me both a free woman and a servant. For I am the servant of your divinity, and I am also the mother of your humanity, O Lord and Son.

Suddenly a servant became a king’s daughter through you, Son of the King. Behold, she who was lowly within David’s house has, because of you, O Son of David—behold, this daughter of earth has reached heaven through the Heavenly One.

How greatly I marvel that there lies before me an infant older than all! His eye is raised toward heaven, while the utterance of his mouth never ceases. It seems to me that his silence speaks with God.
Who has ever seen an infant whose gaze is wholly everywhere? His appearance suggests that he governs all creatures above and below. His gaze resembles that of the Commander who commands everything.
How shall I open a spring of milk for you, the Spring? How shall I give food to you, who feed everyone from your table? How shall I draw near with my breasts to you who are clothed in rays?
To the same tune.

My mouth does not know how to address you, O Son of the Living One. If I dare to call you Joseph’s son, I tremble, for I am not his offspring [?]. And if I deny his name, I am afraid, for my betrothal is to him. Refrain:
Glory to you, Son of the Most High, who took on our body.
Though you are the Son of One, henceforth I shall call you the son of many. They do not suffice for you—many myriads do not suffice for you.
Myriads of names: you are the Son of God, also the Son of Man, also the son of Joseph, also the Son of David, and Mary’s Lord.

Who can [?] the one without a mouth, O Lord of mouths? Because I conceived you, O Pure One, evil men oppressed me. O Holy One, defend your mother! Show mighty deeds, so that they may be convinced from where I conceived you.
Because of you, look, I am hated; Lover of all, look, I am persecuted, because I conceived and bore the one refuge for humankind. Let Adam rejoice, for you are the key to that paradise.
Look, the sea rages against your mother as it did against Jonah. Look, Herod, a raging wave, seeks to drown us. Lord of the seas, where shall I flee? You teach me, Lord of your mother.

With you I will flee, so that through you I may gain life everywhere. A pit with you is no pit, for through you a person ascends to heaven. A grave with you is no grave, for you are also the resurrection.

A star of light suddenly shone in a way beyond its nature, smaller than the sun and greater than the sun. It was smaller than the sun in visible light, but greater than it in hidden power because of the mystery it signified.

The star of the dawn cast its rays into the realm of darkness and led them like blind people. They came and received the great light. They gave offerings and received life; they worshiped and returned.
In the heights and the depths the Son had two heralds: the star of light cried out from above, and John proclaimed from below—two heralds, one earthly and one heavenly.

The one above revealed his nature, that he belongs to majesty; and the one below revealed his nature, that he belongs to humanity. A great wonder: through them both his divinity and his humanity were proclaimed.
Whoever considered him earthly was corrected by the star of light, which showed that he is heavenly. Whoever considered him a spirit was corrected by John, who showed that he also has a body.

In the holy temple Simeon carried him and sang tenderly to him: “You have come, Merciful One, who has compassion on my old age and brings my bones in peace to Sheol. Through you I shall rise from the grave into paradise.”
Anna embraced him and placed her mouth upon his lips, and the Spirit rested upon her lips, as with Isaiah, whose mouth was silent until the coal that was brought near his lips opened his mouth.

Anna grew fervent through the Spirit of his mouth, and she too sang tenderly to him: “Son of royalty, son of lowliness, who hears and remains silent, sees and conceals, knows and hides—God, Son of Man, glory to your name!”

Those who had been childless also heard, ran, and came with their provisions. The Magi came with their treasures; those who had been childless came with their provisions. Provisions and treasures were suddenly heaped up in the home of the poor.

The barren woman cried out, as was her custom: “Who has granted me this, to see your infant, blessed woman, the one who fills heaven and earth? Blessed is your fruit, which brought forth a cluster of grapes in a barren vineyard!”
Zechariah came with his mouth open, exulting and crying out: “Where is the King for whose sake I fathered a voice to proclaim before him? Hail, Son of the King! Our priesthood too is given to you.”
John approached with his parents and worshiped the Son, and radiance rested upon his face. He did not move as he had in the womb. A great wonder: here he worships, and there he leaps!
Herod too, that contemptible fox who strutted about in the lion’s place—the fox lay there and howled when he heard the roar of the lion who had come to lie down over his kingdom, as it is written.

But the fox heard that the lion was a cub, still a nursing infant, and sharpened his fangs so that, while he was still a newborn, the fox might ambush and strangle the lion before he grew strong and the blast of his mouth destroyed him.

All creation acquired mouths and cried out concerning him. The Magi cried out with their offerings; those who had been childless cried out with their children. The star of light cried out in the sky: “Look, the Son of the King!”

The heavens are open, the waters rejoice, the dove is glorious. The Father’s voice resounds more powerfully than thunder and says, “This is my beloved.” The angels announced the good news; the children cried out their hosannas.

At these voices from above and below, they proclaimed and cried out, but she did not stir. Zion slept; at the goad she started. It struck and hurt her; startled, she rose. She killed the Wakeful One because he had awakened her.

The Wakeful One rose from within the tomb, where he had slept while remaining awake. He came and found the nations asleep. He shouted and cried out [and awakened them. Give thanks, you sleepers, to the Wakeful One who has made people wakeful on earth].
To the same tune.

At the Son’s birth there was a great commotion in Bethlehem, for the watchers descended and sang praises there. Their voices became a great thunder in that song of praise. Those who had been silent came and praised the Son. Refrain:
Blessed is the infant through whom Eve and Adam became young again.
The shepherds also came carrying the good things of the flock: sweet milk, pure meat, and fitting praise. They divided them and gave Joseph meat, Mary milk, and the Son praise.

They carried and offered him a suckling lamb: to the Passover Lamb, a firstborn to the Firstborn, a sacrifice to the Sacrifice, a lamb of this passing age to the Lamb of truth. It was a lovely sight, as a lamb was being offered to the Lamb.

The lamb bleated as it was offered before the Firstborn. It gave thanks to the Lamb who came and freed sheep and oxen from sacrifices, and the Passover lamb, which the Son’s Passover came and did away with.
The shepherds approached and bowed before him. With their staffs they greeted him, [prophesying]: “Peace, [O chief of shepherds]! May Moses’ staff give thanks to your staff, Shepherd of all.”
For Moses gives thanks to you: his lambs became wolves, his sheep became like dragons, and his ewes became beasts with fangs. In the fearsome wilderness his flock ran wild and attacked him.

But let the shepherds give thanks to you, for you bring peace between wolves and lambs within the flock. You are the infant who is older than Noah and younger than Noah, who brought peace to all like a [?].
Your father David killed a lion for the sake of a lamb. You, Son of David, are the one who kills the hidden wolf that killed Adam, the innocent lamb who grazed and bleated in that paradise.
At that song of praise the brides stirred and became holy, the virgins became chaste, and the little girls became pure. They hurried and came in throngs and bowed before the Son.

The old women of David’s town came to David’s daughter. They knelt and said, “Blessed is our town, [whose streets have shone] with Jesse’s shoot! [Today David’s throne is established in you, Son of David].”

The old men cried out, “Blessed is the infant who makes Adam young again! Adam grieved when he saw that he had grown old and worn out, while the serpent that killed him shed its skin and became young again. Blessed is the infant through whom Eve and Adam became young again!”

The chaste women said, “Blessed fruit, bless our fruits! Let them be given to you as firstfruits.” They grew fervent and prophesied about their children: when they were killed, they would be plucked for him as firstfruits.

The barren women caressed him as they held him. They fondled him and said, “Blessed fruit conceived without marriage, bless our wombs within marriage! Have mercy on our barrenness, wondrous child of virginity!”
To the same tune.
Blessed is the messenger who came bearing great peace! He brought his Father’s mercy down to us, but did not carry our debts up to him. He reconciled the Lord with those who belong to him. Refrain:
Glory to your divine and human dawning!

Glorious is the Wise One who gave us life! He blended divinity with humanity, one from the height and one from the depth. He mixed the natures like medicines, and there came to be an image: God, a human being.
O zealous one, who saw Adam turned to dust and the accursed serpent devouring him! He dissolved the pungent in the tasteless and made him salt, by which the cursed serpent is blinded.

Blessed is the Merciful One who saw the spear beside Paradise, barring the way to the tree of life, and came and took a body that received the blow, so that through the opening in his side a way might be opened into Paradise.

Glorious is the Merciful One who did not resort to harshness, but triumphed through wisdom without compulsion, to give human beings an example, so that through strength and wisdom they might conquer with discernment.

Blessed is your flock, for you are its gate, you are its staff, you are its shepherd, and you are its drink. You give it salt and care for it. O Only One, who has become fruitful and abundant in every kind of help!

Farmers came and bowed before him. Rejoicing, they prophesied concerning him, the farmer of life: “Blessed is the farmer through whom the soil of the heart is cultivated! He has gathered his wheat into the storehouse of life.”
Cultivators came and gave glory to the shoot that sprang from the root and stump of Jesse: “O virgin cluster of the thirsty vine, may we become vessels for your new wine, which renews everything!”

“Through you may my beloved’s vineyard, which produced wild grapes, be reconciled. Graft its vines with your plants; may the whole vineyard bear blessings. May its fruit appease the owner of the vineyard, who threatened it.”

Carpenters came, because of Joseph, to Joseph’s son: “Blessed is your birth, chief of carpenters, through whom [?] was designed, and through whom [?] too was assembled—the one who establishes time, who entered time!”

“I give thanks on behalf of our craft: may you be our pride! You will make a yoke that is light and easy for those who carry it. You will make a measure in which there can be no fraud, for it is full of truth.”
“You will also construct scales, making them out of justice. On them the negligent are accused, and on them the perfect are acclaimed. On them, O Righteous One, weigh mercies and debts like a judge.”
When Sarah lulled Isaac, he was like a servant bearing the image of the king, his master: on his shoulders was the sign of his wood, and on his hands were bonds and pains, a symbol of the nails.

Rachel cried out to her husband, saying, “Give me children!” Blessed is Mary, who, without asking, received him in holiness into her womb! O his gift, which poured itself out upon those who received it!

Hannah asked for a child with bitter tears; Sarah and Rebekah, with vows and words; and Elizabeth too, through her prayer over a long time—again, through her prayer over a long time. After suffering, then came consolation.

Blessed is Mary, who without vows and without prayer conceived in her virginity and bore the Lord of all the sons of her companions, those who have been and those who are: the chaste and the righteous, priests and kings.
What woman could lull her child in her lap as Mary did? What woman would dare call her son the Son of the Maker, the Son of the Creator? What woman has ever called her son the Son of the Most High?

Bridegrooms rejoiced aloud with brides: “Blessed is the infant whose mother became the bride of holiness! Blessed is the wedding feast where you are present, for even if its wine suddenly runs out, through you it becomes plentiful again.”

Children cried out: “Blessed is the one who became our brother and companion in the streets! Blessed is the day when, with branches, we shall give glory to the tree of life, who bent down from his height to our childhood!”

Women heard, “Look, a virgin will conceive and give birth.” Noblewomen hoped that you would dawn from them, and proud women too, that you would shine forth from them. Blessed is your majesty, which stooped down and dawned from the poor!

Even the little girls who carried him prophesied: “I will belong to you, my Lord. Whether I am ugly or beautiful, and even if I am lowly, I knock for you. I have exchanged the passing bridal chamber for you.”
And because childhood is both bold and talkative, he gathered the little girls, the wise daughters of the Hebrews, and through their lullabies turned laments into prophecy.
To the same tune.

Who would dare speak to her son as his mother does in prayer? He is her hope as God, her beloved and her son as a human being. With fear and love it is fitting for your mother to stand before you.
Refrain:
Glory to you from your flock on the day of your appearing!

You are the Creator’s Son, resembling his Father. As the Maker, he made himself a chaste body in the womb, put it on, and came out. He clothed our weakness in glory through the mercy he brought from his Father.

From Melchizedek, the great priest, hyssop came to you; a throne and crown from the house of David; ancestry and lineage from Abraham. Who could speak to her son this way, as your mother speaks to you?
I became a harbor for you, a great sea. Look, the songs of your father David, together with the words of the prophets, like ships, have unloaded your great wealth beside me.

Your father David wove that psalm of two numbers, a hundred and ten, into a crown for you and brought it. O victorious one, you will be crowned with them, and you will ascend and sit at the right hand.
That number woven from a hundred is a great crown with which your divinity will be crowned. The little crown, the number ten, crowned the head of your humanity, O triumphant one.
For your sake women ran after men. Tamar desired a widower, and Ruth loved an old man. Rahab too, who captured men, was captured by you.
Tamar went out and in darkness stole the Light; in uncleanness she stole holiness; and in nakedness she secretly brought you in, O honored one, who brings forth the chaste from the disreputable.

Satan saw him, grew afraid, and ran to hinder her. He reminded her of judgment, but she was not afraid. She did not dread stoning or the sword. The teacher of adultery was trying to prevent adultery so that he might prevent your coming.
For Tamar’s adultery was holiness for your sake. She thirsted for you, O pure spring. Judah deprived her of [?] your drink. Thirsting for the spring, she stole your drink from his fountain.
She became a widow for your sake; it was you she desired. She ran and became a prostitute too for your sake; it was you she longed for. She waited and became consecrated; it was you she loved.
Let Ruth be thought to have sought your wealth; Moab entered into it [?]. Let Tamar rejoice that her Lord has come, whose name proclaimed the Son of her Lord. Her very name called you to come to her.

For you, honored women made themselves dishonorable. O you who make everyone chaste, it was you she stole at the crossroads. She opened a road to the kingdom of life. She stole, but the sword was powerless to put her to death.

Ruth lay down beside a man on the threshing floor. For your sake her love became bold. For your sake, O teacher of boldness to all who repent, she disregarded every voice that reached her ears for the sake of your voice.

The glowing coal that crept into Boaz’s bed climbed up and lay down. She saw the high priest hidden in his loins, fire for his censer. She ran and became Boaz’s heifer; she bore you, the fattened calf.

She gleaned gleanings for love of you; she gathered stalks. You quickly paid her the wages of her lowliness: instead of ears of grain, a root of kings; and instead of stalks, the sheaf of life that sprang from her.
To the same tune.

When Leah and Rachel, Zilpah and Bilhah sang lullabies to those twelve beloved ones, their children were human, and so were their lullabies. But all your lullabies speak of lordship, O Lord of your brothers.

So that your resurrection too might be believed among unbelievers, they placed you inside a sealed tomb: they sealed the stone, and guards stood watch. It was for your sake that they sealed your tomb, O Son of the Living One.

When they buried you, had they been careless, left you, and gone away, there would have been room to lie that they had stolen you. O giver of life to all, by taking such pains to seal your tomb, they increased your glory.
Daniel too was a type of you, as was Lazarus: one in the pit that the nations sealed, and the other in the tomb that the people opened. Look, their own marks and seals convicted them.

Their mouths would have been open if they had opened your tomb and gone away. By closing your tomb, sealing it, and stamping it, they closed their own mouths. Without realizing it, when they covered your tomb, all the oppressors covered their own heads.

Through your resurrection you convinced them about your birth. The pit was sealed, and the tomb was stamped shut. The innocent one in the pit and the living one in the tomb bore witness to you—the pit and the tomb that had been sealed.

Womb and Sheol, shout and cry out over your resurrection! The womb conceived you while it was sealed; Sheol gave birth to you while it was sealed. Sheol gave birth to you while it was sealed. Contrary to nature, the womb conceived and Sheol gave you up.

The tomb to which they had entrusted the dead man for safekeeping was sealed. The womb that no man had known was virginal. The virgin womb and the sealed tomb cried like trumpets into the ears of the deaf people.

A sealed womb, a stone stamped shut! Among the oppressors they slandered the conception, saying that it came from human seed, and the resurrection, saying that it was a human theft. The seal and the stamp convicted them and convinced them that you are from heaven.

The people stood between your birth and your resurrection and slandered your birth. Your death scorned them; your resurrection refuted them; your birth rebuked them. Two athletes struck the mouth that slandered.

They also went looking for Elijah among the mountains. While they searched for him on earth, this confirmed all the more that he had been taken up. Their search, which did not find him, bore witness that he had been taken up.
If even the prophets who knew of Elijah’s ascent doubted his being taken up, how much more did the impure slander the Son! Through their own guards he convicted them, showing that he had risen.
To the same melody.

Our Lord, no one knows what to call your mother. Shall we call her a virgin? Her child stands before us. A married woman? No man has known her. If your mother cannot be comprehended, who can comprehend you? Refrain:
Praise to you, for whom everything is easy, as the Lord of all.

She alone is your mother, yet she is your sister along with everyone. She became your mother; she became your sister. She is also your betrothed among the chaste women. See, you adorned her in every way—his mother’s beauty [?].
She was betrothed in accordance with nature before you came. But she conceived contrary to nature after you came, O Holy One, and she remained a virgin when she gave birth to you in holiness.

Through you Mary acquired everything belonging to married women: conception within her without intercourse, milk in her breasts contrary to the usual way. Suddenly you made the thirsty ground into a spring of milk.

If she carried you, your great mountain lightened its weight. If she fed you, it was because you had become hungry. If she gave you drink, it was because you had chosen to thirst. If she embraced you, the burning coal of mercy protected her bosom.

Your mother is a wonder! The Lord entered her and became a servant. The Word entered and was silent within her. Thunder entered her and hushed his voice. The Shepherd of all entered; he became a lamb within her and came out bleating.

Your mother’s womb reversed the order of things, O arranger of all. The rich one entered and came out poor. The exalted one entered her and came out humble. Radiance entered her, clothed itself in a lowly appearance, and came out.

The mighty one entered and clothed himself in fear within the womb. The one who feeds all entered and acquired hunger. The one who gives drink to all entered and acquired thirst. The one who clothes all came out of her naked and unclothed.
To the same melody.

Who has ever seen a baby older than the woman who bore him? The Ancient One entered and became a child in her. He came out a newborn and grew on her milk. He entered her small; he came out and grew through her—a great wonder!
Refrain:
Glory on your day to your hidden dawning, and to the Father who sent you.

A baby in the womb, and the seal remains intact! Virginity became a womb for you, a palace for the King, with a virginal doorway over it. Virginity outside and pregnancy within—what great astonishment!
O the chest that was empty and sealed! While it was still sealed, the great Seal of the King of kings came out from within it—a witness crying out that this gift does not come from nature.
Virginity came to womankind because of you, so that your holy conception might be [?]. Your purity dwelt within the seals. The seal rebukes anyone who denies it, claiming that your mother stole.
Even now you dwell within the seal, among chaste women. If anyone slanders your betrothed, the silent seal takes up the dispute against him. The sealed doorway cries out, “Our King is there!”

The seal bears witness for your betrothed and for the woman who bore you. Within the seal you dwelt in your mother and in chaste women, within the seal’s impression. May your seal vindicate your betrothed as it did your mother.

For this is a great holiness that is not believed among the impure. The seal and signet of the King of kings give assurance that the pearl is protected. Your maidservants have acquired good advocates among their slanderers.
If that treasury is not trusted even with a seal, who could have believed, without a seal’s impression, that it had not been plundered? God has given humanity assurance on behalf of his holy ones.

You dwelt in Mary, and the impure slandered her, saying that she had not conceived you. Now that you dwell among chaste women, look, they are slandered as though they were pregnant. They slandered both the one who conceived and the one who did not conceive—a great grief!
Your wall protects your betrothed as it did your mother. If a thief comes to steal, may he be thwarted by you and driven away. If a slanderer comes to slander, may he be silenced by you.

Praise to you, who purify your flock as you did your mother, your chaste women as you did the woman who bore you, and your maidservants as you did the woman who nursed you. From them and from her, and from all of us, glory to your name!
To the same tune.

The Hebrew women who read Jeremiah’s laments recited praises from their scrolls instead of the laments in their books. A hidden power was prophesying through their words.
Refrain:
From everything you have created, praise to you on this feast of yours!

For they answered and said, “Let Eve rejoice today in Sheol, for her daughter’s son has come down like a life-giving medicine to raise his mother’s mother to life. The blessed infant crushes the head of the serpent that struck her.”
Your image peered out from the childhood of lovely Isaac. Through you Sarah sang to him when she saw your mysteries resting upon his infancy: “O son of my vows, in whom the Lord of vows is hidden!”
Samson the Nazirite portrayed an image of your might when he tore apart the lion, a likeness of death. You tear death apart and bring out of its bitterness sweet life for humanity.
Hannah too loved Samuel because of you. Your justice was hidden in him when he cut Agag to pieces as he would the Evil One. He wept over Saul, for your grace too was portrayed in him.
How humble you are! How mighty you are, O newborn child! Your judgment is mighty; your love is sweet. Who can fathom you? Your Father is in heaven and your mother on earth. Who can describe you?
If anyone seeks your hidden nature, there it is in heaven, in the vast bosom of the Godhead. If anyone seeks your visible body, there it lies, peeping out from Mary’s little lap.
The mind is bewildered among your stories, O rich one: dense folds in your divinity, lowly appearances in your humanity. Who can fathom you, great sea that made itself small?
We come to see you as God, and look—you are a human being! We come to see you as a human being, and the sign of your divinity shines forth. Who can understand your changes, O true one?

[We come to see] the dwelling allotted to you from the house of David. A manger is what you inherited from his beds; a cave fell to your lot from his palaces. Instead of his chariot, a lowly foal [?] falls to your lot.
Who would believe that you inherited David’s throne? We went to scorn you, but at a roar from you, heaven and the earth beneath cried out. After we had scorned you, a hidden power bowed before you.
How bold you are, infant, throwing yourself upon everyone! Look, you laugh at everyone who sees you. Look, you yearn! Your love is like that of someone hungry for human beings.
Do you not distinguish your parents from strangers, your mother from other mothers, or your nursing mother from unclean women? Is it your boldness, or is it your love that loves everyone?
