How restless you are, throwing yourself upon everyone who sees you! You cling to the rich and the poor, though they have not called you. Where did you get this hunger for human beings?

What is this love of yours? If someone rebukes you, you do not become angry; if someone shouts at you, you are not alarmed; if someone quarrels with you, you are not saddened. Surely you are greater than the law that repays injuries!

Moses was meek, but his zeal was fierce: he struck out and killed. Elisha too, who brought a boy to life, tore apart a crowd of children through bears. Who are you, child, whose love is greater than that of the prophets?

That son of Hagar, who was a wild donkey, kicked Isaac. Isaac endured it in silence, but his mother grew indignant. Are you his mystery, or is he your foreshadowing? Do you resemble Isaac, or is it rather he who resembles you?
To the same tune.

Come, rest and be still in your mother’s bosom, noble son. Boldness does not suit the sons of kings. You are the son of that noble David, and the son of Mary, who guarded her beauty in the inner chamber.
Refrain:
Praise to you, who on this day brought joy to everyone!

Whom does this cheerful infant resemble, this lovely child whose mother is chaste and whose Father is hidden, whom not even the seraphim can see? Whom do you resemble? Tell us, Son of the Merciful One!

You made the angry people who came to look at you rejoice; they mingled their laughter with one another’s. The spiteful became sweet through you, O sweet one. Who are you, child, through whom even the bitter become sweet?
Who has ever seen an infant who longs for those nearby from within the lap, and reaches out toward those far away? A lovely sight: an infant who coaxes everyone with his whole being to look at him!

Someone who had worries came and saw you, and his worries fled. Someone who was brooding saw you and forgot his brooding through you. Through you the hungry person forgot even his food, and someone sent on an errand was captivated by you and forgot his journey.

Be still yourself, and release people to their tasks! You are a son of the poor. [?] the livelihood of all the poor who stopped work and came. Lover of humanity, you have wearied people with your cheerfulness.
That noble King David took branches, and at the festival, as he danced among the children, he gave praise. Could it be that the love of David your father is now boiling within you?

Her father’s demon spoke through that daughter of Saul. She called that noble man contemptible, though he gave the elders of the people an example: to take branches together with the children on the day you are acclaimed.

Who would not fear to charge you with being shameless? Look: Saul’s daughter, who poured out wickedness, cut off her womb from childbearing because her mouth mocked. Her barrenness was the reward of her mouth.

Let mouths tremble at blaspheming you, lest they be shut. Daughter of Zion, guard your mouth against that Son of David who rejoices before you. Do not become like Saul’s daughter, whose line came to an end.
God saw how the unclean people were both adulterous and jealous, and how oppressive they were. He had compassion on the women. For our sake he multiplied his provisions among the oppressors.

If her husband hated her, he was to write a document and release her; if he was jealous of her, the water was to test her; and if he accused her unjustly, God provided the sheet. Every accusation was put to shame beside Mary, who remained sealed.

Moses exposed them beforehand, showing how oppressive they were: although the sheets proving the virgins’ virginity were with their husbands, they accused them and killed them. How greatly, then, they wronged the Son’s mother!

Through the testing waters and the sheets he was instructing them, so that when the Lord of all pregnancies came, and they accused the womb in which he dwelt unjustly, its pure virginity would persuade them about him on account of her pregnancy.

If, then, the signs of virginity that were brought out rescued a married woman from the sword, guard it and be guarded, wise women! It is a weapon that, if defeated, turns back and fights against its owner.
Elijah, who suppressed his body’s desire, withheld rain from adulterers. Because he had dried up his body, he dried up the dew for the sexually immoral, who had loosened and let their springs flow.
Because the hidden fire of bodily desire had not ruled over him, the fire from on high obeyed him. Because he conquered fleshly desire on earth, he ascended to where holiness dwells in stillness.

Elisha too, who put his body to death, brought a dead person to life. Through holiness he brought natural mortality to life; beyond nature he revived the child whose life had sunk away as though exhausted.

Moses, who divided and separated himself from his wife, divided the sea. In contrast to the adulteress, Zipporah kept chastity, although she was a priest’s daughter; Abraham’s daughter committed adultery with the calf.
To the same tune.

In you I will begin, and I trust that in you I will finish. I will open my mouth, and you fill my mouth. I am soil for you, and you are the farmer. Sow your voice in me, you who sowed yourself in my mother’s womb.
Refrain:
Glory to you, my Lord, and through you to your Father, on the day of your birth!

All chaste women marvel at me—the daughters of the Hebrews and the virgins, the daughters of rulers. Because of you I am envied, though I am a daughter of the poor; because of you I arouse jealousy, though I am a daughter of the lowly. Who gave you to me?

Son of the Rich One, who rejected the embrace of rich women, who drew you to the poor? Joseph is needy, and I am destitute. Your merchants loaded their goods and brought gold to the house of the poor.

She saw the Magi, and her songs multiplied because of their offerings: “Look, your worshipers surround me, and your offerings encircle me!” Blessed is the infant who made his mother a lyre for his songs!

As a lyre looks to its master, my mouth looks to you. Let your will move your mother’s tongue. Just as I learned through you a new conception, let my mouth learn through you a new birth of new praise.

If difficult things are not difficult for you, but are easy—a womb conceived you without intercourse, and without seed a womb bore you—then it is easy for a mouth to bear fruit and multiply your great praise.

Look, I am wronged and mistreated, yet I rejoice. My ears are full of reproach and mockery, but whatever I endure is a small thing to me, for one consolation from you can drive away countless afflictions.

My face shows that I am not disgraced because of you, my son, and that I have been wronged. I conceived and gave birth to Truth, who vindicates me. For if Tamar was vindicated through Judah, how much more shall I be vindicated through you!
David your father sang a song to you before you came, saying that gold from Sheba would be offered to you. The song he sang in bare words is now made real: myrrh and gold are heaped before you.

The hundred and fifty songs he sang were seasoned with you. All the words of prophecy need
your savor, for without your salt,
your savor, for without your salt,
all wisdom is tasteless.
To the same tune.

I will not be jealous, my son, that you should be with everyone as well as with me. Be God to whoever acknowledges you; be Lord to whoever serves you; and be a brother to whoever loves you, so that you may give life to all.

When you dwelt in me, your majesty dwelt both within me and outside me. And when I visibly gave birth to you, your hidden power still did not leave me. You are within me and you are outside me, you who astound your mother.
When I see your outward image before my eyes, your hidden image is drawn in my mind. In your visible image I saw Adam, and in the hidden one I saw your Father, who is united with you.

Was it to me alone that you showed your beauty in two images? Let bread portray you, and the mind as well. Dwell in the bread and in those who eat it. In what is hidden and what is visible, may your church see you as your mother does.

Whoever hates your bread is like someone who hates your body. Even someone far away who loves your bread is close to the one who loved your image. In bread and body, both the earlier and the later generations have seen you.

Your bread, child, is indeed far more precious than your body. For even unbelievers saw your body, but they do not see your living bread. Those far away rejoiced: their portion surpassed that of those nearby.

Look, your image is painted in the blood of grapes above the bread, and painted on the heart by the finger of love with the pigments of faith. Blessed is he who did away with carved images through the image of his truth!

You are not a man whom I could portray in an ordinary way, for your conception is unprecedented and your birth is a wonder. Without the Spirit, who can sing to you? Look, a new utterance of prophecy is welling up within me.
How can I call you a stranger to us, you who came from us? Shall I call you Son? Shall I call you Lord, you who give your mother another birth from the waters?

I am your sister, for I come from the house of David, who is father to us both. I am also your mother because I conceived you, and your betrothed because you made me holy; a maidservant and a daughter of blood and water—you purchased and baptized me.

The Son of the Most High came and dwelt in me, and I became his mother. Just as I gave birth to him, he too gave me another birth. A twofold birth: his body put on his mother's clothing, and I put on his glory.

Amnon dishonored Tamar, who was of the house of David, and virginity fell from the house they shared and was lost. My pearl was not lost: it is laid up in your treasury, for you have clothed yourself in it.
Let all your brides' virginities [be preserved for you]. They are purple robes, and no one is permitted to approach them except our King. Virginity is like a veil for you, High Priest.

The scent of her father-in-law wafted from Tamar, for she had stolen his perfumes. But from the clothing of Joseph's betrothed not even a breath of lust wafted when she conceived. Your conception became a wall of fire for me, Son of the Holy One.

The blossom faded, for the fragrance of the Lily of Glory was strong. The treasury of perfumes had no need of the flower or its fragrances. The flesh kept its distance when it saw in the womb a conception by the Spirit.
A woman serves before the man who is her head. Joseph stood to serve before his Lord, who was within Mary. He served as a priest before your ark because of your holiness.

Moses carried the stone tablets on which his Lord had written, and Joseph reverently carried the pure tablet in which the Creator’s Son dwelt. The tablets were left behind, for the world was filled with your teaching.
To the same tune.

“The infant whom I carry carried me,” Mary said. “He lowered his wings, lifted me, and placed me between his wings. He rose into the air and promised me, ‘The heights and the depths shall belong to you.’” Refrain:
Glory to you, Son of the Creator, who loves everyone.
I saw Gabriel call him Lord, and the aged servant reverently carry the high priest. I saw the Magi bowing down, and Herod bewildered because the King had come.

Satan, who strangled children to destroy Moses, kills children so that the Living One may die. I will flee to Egypt, so that he who came to Judah may toil and be bewildered, seeking to hunt his own hunter.

In her virginity Eve clothed herself in leaves of shame. In her virginity your mother clothed herself in a robe of glory. To him who provides for everyone I gave a little covering of flesh—to him who clothes everything.

Blessed is she in whose heart and mind you dwell! Through you, Son of the King, she is a royal citadel, and a Holy of Holies for you, the high priest. She has neither anxiety nor the cares of a house and husband.

Eve also became a pit and a grave for the cursed serpent, whose evil counsel entered and dwelt in her. She became food for him when she became dust. You are our bread, and you are our bridal chamber and our robe of glory.

For the woman who possesses holiness, if she is afraid, here is its guardian. For the woman who has sin, here is its forgiver. For the woman who has a demon, here is its pursuer. For their pains, here is the one who binds up their wounds.

Let the woman who has a son have him come and become a brother to my beloved. Whoever has a daughter or a female relative, let her come and become the betrothed of my precious one. Whoever has a slave, let him release him to come and serve his Lord.

The freeborn man who takes up your yoke, my son, has one reward. But the slave who carries a pair of yokes belonging to two masters, the one above and the one below, has two blessings and two rewards for his two burdens.

The freeborn woman, my son, is also your servant if she serves you. The enslaved woman is free through you. Let her take comfort in you, for she has been set free. Hidden freedoms are laid in her bosom if she loves you.

You chaste women, long for my beloved, so that he may dwell in you; and you unclean women, so that he may sanctify you; and you churches, so that he may adorn you. He is the Creator’s Son, who has come to examine all created things.

He renewed the heavens, all of whose lights fools worshiped. He renewed the earth, which had grown old in Adam. Through his spittle it became a new creation. He who provides for everyone restores bodies along with minds.

Come, blind people, and receive light without money! Come, lame people, receive your feet! Stammerers and mute people, receive your voices! Those whose hands are withered, let the withered receive their hands as well!

He is the Creator’s Son, whose treasuries are full of every kind of help. Let anyone who needs pupils for his eyes come to him. He makes mud and transforms it into flesh; he makes eyes and gives them light.

With a little mud he showed that our dust was fashioned by his hand. The soul of the dead also testified for him that the breath of humanity was breathed in by him. Through the later witnesses he was confirmed as the Son of the First One.

Gather and come, lepers, and receive cleansing without labor! There is no need, as with Elisha, to bathe seven times in the river. Nor does he impose the labor that priests undertook with their sprinklings.

Elisha’s seven washings cleansed through the mystery of the seven spirits. The hyssop and the blood are a great symbol. There is no place for estrangement: the Son of the Lord of all is not estranged from the Lord of all.

For if the Just One made the body leprous, and you cleanse it, O Maker of the body, he hated the body while you loved it. Yet you formed it! The sufferings you laid upon it cry out that you are the Creator’s Son.
To the same tune.

In the years of the king whom they called by the name of Radiance, our Lord dawned among the Hebrews. Radiance and Dawn reigned and came: the king on earth and the Son on high. Blessed is his dominion! [Refrain:
Glory to you, who have brought joy to everyone at this feast!]

In the days of the king who registered people for the poll tax, our Savior came down and registered people in the book of life. He registered others, and they registered him. On high he registered us; on earth they registered him. Glory to his name!
His birth was in the days of the king whose name was [Radiance]: king and King, Radiance and Dawn. That kingdom bore his cross. [Blessed is he who raised it!]
For thirty years [he remained on earth] in poverty. My brothers, let us weave sounds of praise with all our discernment: for our Lord’s years, for thirty years, thirty crowns. Blessed is his birth!

In the new year, rich in treasures and full of blessings, let the cherubim who bore the Son in glory give thanks with us. He left his glorious praise, toiled, and found the sheep that was lost. To him be thanksgiving!

In the second year, let the seraphim who proclaimed the Son holy give abundant thanks with us. They turned and saw him being insulted among unbelievers. He endured mockery and taught praise. To him be glory!
In the third year, let Michael’s company give thanks with us. They served the Son on high and saw him serving on earth. He washed feet and cleansed souls. Blessed is his humility!

In the fourth year, let heaven give thanks with us. In its entirety it is too small for the Son, and it marveled to see him reclining on the couch of despised Zacchaeus. He occupied a couch and filled heaven. To him be greatness!

In the fifth year, let the sun, which scorches the earth with its heat, give thanks to our Sun. He lowered his intensity and tempered his strength so that the weak eye of the hidden soul could bear to see him. Blessed is his radiance!
In the sixth year, let all the air also give thanks with us. Though it prides itself on its vastness, it saw its great Lord become a little infant in a little lap. Blessed is his glory!

In the seventh year, let clouds and winds shout joyfully with us and sprinkle dew on the faces of blossoms. They saw the Son subdue his splendor and accept dishonor and filthy spittle. Blessed is his salvation!
Again, in the eighth year, let creation offer praise, whose fruits suck nourishment from its springs. It bowed down when it saw the Son in a lap, the pure one drinking pure milk. Blessed is his will!
In the ninth year, let the earth offer praise. Only when its barren womb is watered does it bear fruit. It saw Mary, a thirsty land, whose fruit was a great sea. To him be exaltation!

In the tenth year, let Mount Sinai offer praise, which melted before its Lord. It saw them take up stones against its Lord. He accepted stones so that he might build his church upon stones. Blessed is his building!

In the eleventh year, let the great sea give thanks to the hollow of the Son’s hand, which measured it. It marveled to see him descend and be baptized in a little water, cleansing creatures. Blessed is his victory!

In the twelfth year, let the holy temple give thanks, which saw the child sitting among the elders. The dark ones [?] fell silent when the Lamb of the feast bleated at his feast. Blessed is his atonement!

In the thirteenth year, let crowns give thanks with us to the King who triumphed and was crowned with a crown of thorns. He bound a great crown upon Adam at his right hand. Blessed is the one who sent him!

In the fourteenth year, let the Passover of Egypt give thanks to the Passover who came and brought joy to everyone. In place of Pharaoh, he drowned Legion; in place of the horsemen, he drowned the demons. Blessed is his recompense!

In the fifteenth year, let the lamb of the flock give thanks, for our Lord did not slaughter it as Moses did. He redeemed humankind by his own blood. He, the shepherd of all, died for all. Blessed is the one who begot him.
In the sixteenth year, let the wheat give thanks symbolically to that farmer who sowed his body in barren earth, which sprouted beyond every [?] and yielded new bread. Blessed is the victorious one.

In the twenty-seventh year, let the vine give thanks to our Lord, the true vineyard. Souls became like planted shoots. He brought peace to the vineyard and laid waste the vineyard that yielded carobs. Blessed is the one who uprooted it.

In the seventeenth year, let the vine that the wild boar devoured give thanks to the true vineyard, which cultivated itself, guarded its fruit, and offered fruit to the owner of the vineyard. Blessed is its cultivator.
23. In the eighteenth year, let our leaven give thanks to the true leaven, which penetrated and drew together all minds, making them one mind through one teaching. Blessed is your teaching.

In the nineteenth year, let salt give thanks to your body, blessed child. The soul is the salt of the body, and faith is the salt of the soul, through which it is preserved. Blessed is your protection.

In the twentieth year, let worldly wealth give thanks with us. Perfect men neglected and abandoned it because of the woe, and came to love poverty because of its blessedness. Blessed is the one who chose it.

In the twenty-first year, let the waters that were sweetened through the mystery of the Son give thanks. In Samson’s honey the nations tasted bitterness, for he destroyed them. They came to life through the cross, which redeemed them. Blessed is your sweetness.

In the twenty-second year, let weapons and swords give thanks. They could not kill our adversary; you were the one who killed him. You were also the one who reattached the ear that Simon’s sword cut off. Blessed is your healing.

In the twenty-third year, let the donkey also give thanks, for she bore a colt on which the opener of mouths could ride. He also gave a song of praise to the wild asses, Hagar’s offspring. Blessed is your song of praise.

In the twenty-fourth year, let wealth give thanks to the Son. Treasuries marveled at the Lord of treasuries as he grew up among the poor. He made himself poor to enrich everyone. Blessed is your fellowship with us.

In the twenty-fifth year, let Isaac give thanks to the Son, who spared him from the knife on the mountain and became a lamb for slaughter in his place. The mortal escaped, and the giver of life to all died. Blessed is his offering.

In the twenty-sixth year, let Moses, who was afraid and fled from killers, give thanks with us. Let him give thanks to the Son, who entered Sheol on his own feet, plundered it, and came out. Blessed is your resurrection.
In the twenty-seventh year, let eloquent advocates give thanks to the Son. They could find no way for our case to be won. He forgave—there is no judgment—and won our case. Praise be to him.

In the twenty-seventh year, let all judges who put wrongdoers to death as just men give thanks. Let them give thanks to the Son, who, being good, died in place of the wicked, though he is the Son of the Just One. Blessed are his mercies.

In the twenty-eighth year, let all mighty warriors give thanks to the Son. They did not deliver us from the captor. The one who is worshiped, who became a slaughtered victim, overtook him and delivered us. Blessed is your deliverance.
In the twenty-ninth year, let Job, who endured sufferings for his own sake, give thanks with us. Our Lord endured spitting and lashes, thorns and nails for our sake. Blessed is his compassion.

In the thirtieth year, let the dead who came to life through his death give thanks with us, along with the living who turned back through his crucifixion, and the heights and depths that were reconciled through him. Blessed [?] are he and his Father.
The hymns for the Nativity of our Lord, composed by the blessed Mar Ephrem, are finished. Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and at all times, and forever and ever. Amen.
The twelfth. To the same tune.

Uzziah, Jotham, and Ahaz were defeated in their wars. In exchange for the captives who went down to Assyria, the Magi came to us with good news. The sweet fragrance of their spices spread through our streets.
Refrain:
Praise to you, Son of the Lord of all, who gives life to all!

Because you are the Son of the Merciful One, your kindness showed them mercy. Because you are the Son of the Jealous One, your might called them to account. Because you are the Son of the Rich One, in keeping with their love they made restitution for the harm they had done through their offerings.

You blended these together so that you would not grieve us, yet would give them life. Those who carried off our silver brought gold. Those who struck our bodies brought myrrh. Those who burned our sanctuary offered frankincense to your divinity.

Their myrrh pleads on behalf of their swords, with which they killed us. Their gold pleads on behalf of our treasures, for they plundered the treasuries of Hezekiah's house. Their frankincense appeases your divinity, for they angered your Father.

Ahaz sent to the Assyrian, saying, “Come up and rescue me!” Those who had been brought low were exalted through you. They came to you with their gifts in exchange for Jeconiah, the hostage whom they took captive from the house of David.

Through his envoys Ahaz subjected himself to Assyria. Through you they subjected themselves by their envoys. The tribe of the lion's cub had bowed down; to you, the one worthy of worship, the mighty who had received worship bowed down.

When Aram and Ephraim marched and came up, Zion feared that she would be left widowed of the house of David. Ahaz abandoned her and fled, but Isaiah went out and gave her the good news of you: “God is with us!”

“Look,” he said, “the virgin will conceive and give birth without intercourse.” Is this a dream for me, or a fable? For here on my knees is Emmanuel! I will put everything else aside and give thanks to the Lord of all every day.

Those who dishonored virgins in Zion honored your mother, O virgin child, who clothed himself in his mother's virginity and came forth with it. To me you are a child, a bridegroom, a son, and also God.

The Babylonians also came up and dashed children to pieces in Judah. Through you, newborn children were safe. Through you, evildoers became worshipers. Those who dishonored the elderly honored the child who is older than all.
Babylon also sent gifts to Hezekiah. The envoys marveled when they saw his treasures. What did you show the Magi? You showed a wonder, for they worshiped you although you were poor.

Although the ivory palace of the kings of our people was great, the little enclosure in which I gave birth to you is greater and more beautiful than it. Amid the thickets the shepherds saw your glory.

If someone of lowly nature puts on a crown, he is exalted by the crown. Your nature is great, O son of the poor, and through you whatever is lowly is exalted. Even if someone places thorns on your head, they are like a crown.
A lowly body is adorned with beryls. In you even lowly things are precious and become beautiful. Whatever is joined to you is great. Even if someone throws a stone at you, it is a pearl.

Even your sweat is baptism for whoever is worthy. The dust of your clothes is, for whoever is sick, the greatest source of every kind of help. Even if your spittle reaches someone's face, it gives light to the eyes.
If you rest your head on a stone, they divide it and snatch it up. If you sleep on a dunghill, it becomes a church for prayers. And if you break ordinary bread, it is the medicine of life for us.

Who can insult you, when even your humiliation is a blessing to the nations? Who can put you to death, when even your death is full of life for humanity? Even if you go up and mount the wood, you are the Passover lamb.

For your mountain is greater than the one who bore you. Let me sit and rest; be a harbor for me. The great Nature that cannot be described has taken refuge in you. Allow your mother to fall silent about you, for her mouth is weary.

Withhold your gift from your harp, so that it may rest a little, for you have taught me. Everything I have said, you taught me. How can I fall silent, since you have wearied me? Give me rest yourself. Glory to your Father!
The sixteenth. To the same melody.

Because of you Sarah became jealous of the boy’s mother, contrary to her custom. She was not jealous where even chaste women are jealous; she was jealous over a slave because of you, O freeborn Son. Refrain:
From Sarah’s household and from the nations, praise to you!

Because of your appearing, Isaac prayed for his wife. She conceived a wolf and a lamb together. He showed that Abraham does not have many blessed descendants: his offspring who blesses everyone is one.
If Abraham has many blessed descendants, look at Esau and Ishmael! They are the firstborn of Abraham’s household. Through two accursed ones he showed that the blessed offspring is one.

Sarah loved you, the King’s Son, and hated the king. A royal household did not please her; she wandered about with an exile and became his companion, because she saw your appearing, which was hidden in him.
[?] Ninety years did not weary her as she waited for you. You came to Sarah when she was ninety, and you came to Abraham when he was a hundred. You gave [?]
Change of melody. Response: Blessed is the limitless one who became small, to make us great without limit.
Let us speak about the birth of the Firstborn on his feast. On his day he gives hidden help. If an unclean man, at his feast and at the commemoration
of his birthday, gave a wrathful gift—a head on a platter—how many blessings will the Blessed One give to whoever sings at his feast!
Let us not count our vigil like the vigils of every day. It is a festival whose reward is a hundred times greater. For it is a feast that battles against
sleep through its vigil. It is a speaker that battles against silence with its voice. Clothed in every blessing, it is a mighty commander of feasts, rich in joys.
Today angels and archangels came down and sang a new song of praise on earth. In that same mystery they descend and rejoice with those who keep vigil,
exulting. At the time when they sang praise, the world was full of blasphemy. Blessed is the birth through which the world now resounds with songs of praise!
For this is the night that mingles the Watchers above with the vigils. The Watcher came to make watchers within creation. Those who keep vigil have now been made
partners of the Watchers. Those who sing praise have become companions of the seraphim. Blessed is whoever has become a harp for your praise and whose reward has been your mercy!
Let us sing to him about the birth of the Firstborn: how the Divinity wove itself a garment in the womb, put it on, and came forth in birth. In death
it took it off again. Once it took it off; twice it put it on. It wrapped itself in it on the left, removed it from there, and placed it on the right.
The Power that governs everything dwelt in a little womb. While he dwelt there, he was loosening everyone’s bonds. He obeyed the one who begot him, so that he might fulfill his will.
Heaven and all created things were filled with him. The sun entered the womb, while his rays dwelt in the heights and the depths.
He dwelt in the spacious bosoms of all created things, yet they are too small to contain the greatness of the Firstborn. How, then, did
Mary’s womb have room for him? It is a wonder if it had room for him [?]. Of all the bosoms that held him, one bosom had room for him: that of the Great One who begot him.
The womb that held him, if it held him entirely, is equal to that wondrous bosom which is greater than the one that bore him. And who would dare to say that it is equal
A small womb, weak and despised, although the great Being dwelt there because of his mercy; and although his nature is great, he was not confined by anything.
Reconciling peace sent to the nations; a gladdening radiance that came to the sorrowful; powerful leaven that conquers everything
quietly; the patient one who wins over creation one by one. Blessed is whoever has lodged your joys in his heart and forgotten his troubles in you.
The mouths of the Watchers cried out peace to those keeping watch. The good news brought by the Watchers reached those keeping watch. Who could sleep on this night
that awakened creation? For they proclaimed peace where there had been anger. Blessed is the infant who by his silence reconciled the Majesty whom speaking beings had angered.

The Watchers mingled with those keeping watch and rejoiced that the world had been given life. The evil one was put to shame, who had made himself king and put on a false crown. He had set up his throne like God
in the world. The infant lying in the manger cast him down from his dominion. The sun returned the worship: through its Magi it honored him; through its worshipers they worshiped him.
God had seen that people worshiped created things. He clothed himself in a created body to win us over through our own custom. Look, through this thing formed, our Former
healed us; and through this created thing our Creator gave us life. His force did not lead us. Blessed is he who came in what is ours and mingled us with what is his.
O you who are greater than measure, who became small beyond measure! From glorious splendor you descended to lowliness. The mercies brought you down all this way,
which dwell in you. Bend your compassion toward me; be praised through my wickedness. Blessed is whoever became a fountain of voices and gave thanks with his whole being to all of you.
He became a servant on earth; he was Lord on high. He inherited the height and the depth, he who became a stranger. He whom they judged unjustly became a judge in truth.
He into whose face they spat breathed the spirit into faces. He who held a feeble reed became a staff for the world, which had grown old and leaned upon him.
He who stood and served the servants is worshiped as he sits. He whom the scribes mocked—the seraphim proclaimed his holiness before him. This is the glory Adam wanted to steal
secretly. The serpent saw to what height the one he had overthrown was raised. He crushed him because he had deceived him. Eve's feet trampled him who had poured bitterness into her ears.
The barren woman had marital relations and longed for fruit, but Mary's womb conceived in holiness. One should marvel at the fields, and at the plantings

be amazed. The former withheld what she had received, while the latter returned what she had not borrowed. Nature acknowledged that it had lost its case: a womb had withheld from it, while another repaid it what it had not given her.
Through Elizabeth, Mary was vindicated in judgment. Barrenness demonstrated that the will which was able to close an open door also opened the closed one.
He opened it. A barren womb [?]; he made a virgin womb fruitful. Because the people were unbelieving, he made the married woman a barrier against accusations directed at the pure woman.
He who was able made barren, lifeless breasts flow. He dried them up when they were young and made them flow when they had grown old. He compelled and changed nature in its proper season
and outside its proper season. The Lord of natures changed the virgin's nature. Because the people were barren, he made the old woman a mouthpiece for the young woman.
As he began with birth, he continued and finished with death. His birth received worship; his death paid the debt. Just as he came to birth and the Magi
worshiped him, so again he came to suffering, and the robber took hold of him. Between his birth and his death he placed the world in the middle; through birth and death he gave it life.
Change of melody. Response: Blessed is he by everyone at his birth. Blessed is he by everyone [?] at his birth. A 1. Give thanks, nations, at the feast, the firstborn of all feasts.
Recount the sufferings that existed, the wounds and the pains, so that we may know what wound the Child who was sent healed. Blessed is he who was sufficient for our pains. A 2. Give thanks, nations.

The redeemed, to the Redeemer of all at his birth. My weak tongue too became a harp through mercy, to sing the victories of the Firstborn at his festival. Blessed is he who made us worthy of his feast.
Aleph. 3. How indeed can anyone marvel at the physician unless he hears and learns what pains there were? When our wound is proclaimed, then our physician is exalted. Blessed

is he who triumphed through our pains. Beth. 4. Created things were worshiped because the worshiper was foolish. He worshiped everything, because they did not worship the One. The Merciful One came down and broke the yoke

that had enslaved everyone. Blessed is he who released us from our yoke. Gimel. 5. The mercies of the Most High were revealed, and he came down and freed his creation in this blessed month, in which freedom is granted
The Lord came to servitude to call slaves to freedom. Blessed is he who brought freedom. Gimel. 6. The Lord of the months chose two months for his events. His

conception took place in Nisan, and his birth in Kanun. In Nisan he sanctified those conceived, and in Kanun he freed those born. Blessed is he who brought joy through his months. Gimel. 7. The sun cried out in silence

to its Lord about those who worshiped it. The servant grieved because it was worshiped instead of its Lord. Now creation is joyful because the Creator is worshiped. Blessed is the worshipful Child. Gimel. 8.

Three months wove a crown and crowned him with victories. The blessed month served his birth, and the lovely month his resurrection. For his blessed ascension, the months carried crowns and crowned him. Blessed
is he who triumphed through his months. Gimel. 9. Smile, creation; brighten your face at our feast. Let the church sing aloud, and heaven and earth in silence. Sing and give thanks to the Child

who brought freedom for all. Blessed is he who canceled our debt certificates. Daleth. 10. The fools who honored the sun dishonored it by their honor. Now that they know it is a servant, as it runs its course
its Lord is worshiped. All the servants rejoice that they are counted as servants. Blessed is he who set the natural orders in place. He. 11. We acted perversely, for we became slaves. Look,
our freedom compelled the servant to become our lord. The sun, the servant of all, we made lord of all. Blessed is he who turned us back to himself. Waw. 12. The moon too, which was worshiped,
was freed at his birth. For it is a marvel that the light which illuminates the eyes darkened the eyes that looked upon it as a god. Blessed is the ray
that enlightened us. Zain. 13. Fire was vindicated by your birth, which freed it from worship. The Magi who bowed down before you had worshiped it. They abandoned it and worshiped its Lord,
exchanging fire for fire. Blessed is he who baptized us in his light. Heth. 14. Instead of the foolish fire that consumes its own body, the Magi worshiped the fire that gave
its body to those who eat. The burning coal drew near and sanctified unclean lips. Blessed is he who mingled his fire with us. Teth. 15. Error blinded people so that they would worship created things

Fellow servants were worshiped, and the Lord of all was denied his due. The One worthy of worship came down to be born and gathered worship to himself. Blessed is he who was worshiped by all. Yodh. 16. The Knower

of all saw that we worshiped things that were made. He put on a body that was made, to catch us through our own habit, so that through a body that was made he might draw us to the Creator. Blessed is he who devised a way

and drew us. Yodh. 17. The Evil One knew how to harm us: through the heavenly lights he blinded us; through possessions he injured us; through gold he impoverished us. Through the sculptor’s carved images he made a heart of stone

for us. Blessed is he who came and softened it. Kaph. 18. They carved stones, and he arranged for people to stumble over them. They did not put them on the road so that the blind would stumble over them.
They called them gods so that the sighted would stumble over them. Blessed is he who exposed the idols. Kaph. 19. Sin spread its wings to cover everything, so that not

A person can truly look above himself. Truth descended into the womb; he came out and rolled error away. Blessed is he who folded it up by his birth.
Lamed — 20.
For he could not

bear it—the Merciful One who saw that they had blocked the road. As he descended into the womb, he opened the road a little; when he came out, he cleared it and fixed his milestones along it. Blessed is he

who made your road safe.
Lamed — 21.
He chose the prophets to clear the road for the people; he sent the apostles to smooth the path for the nations. The evil one's stumbling blocks were put to shame,

because the weak cleared them away. Blessed is he who made our paths level.
Mem — 22.
The carved images were secretly blinding their carvers. They carved an eye in stone and blinded the eyes

of the soul. Thanks to your birth, which gave sight to blind seers! Blessed is he who restored sight.
Nun Nun — 23.
Let women give thanks to that pure Mary, for through Eve their mother

their disgrace had been great. Look, through Mary their sister their triumph has grown! Blessed is he who dawned from them.
Nun Nun — 24.
Let the nations give thanks to your birth, through which they gained eyes

to see. Their wine released its grip on them, and they saw their own degradation. They judge themselves and worship the one who rescued them. Blessed is he who taught repentance.
Samekh — 25.

Humanity scattered its worship everywhere. It did not wish to offer worship to the one worthy of worship. Yet the objects of worship could not bear it from the worshipers who went astray. Blessed is he

who descended and was worshiped.
Samekh — 26.
The image-makers' gold worshiped you, for you drew it toward charitable gifts. It had lain idle among the dead, away from the needs of the living. It ran to your money chest,

just as it ran to your manger. Blessed is he whom creation loved.
Samekh — 27.
The frankincense that had served demons worshiped your birth. It had been sorrowful in its fragrance; it rejoiced when it saw

its Lord. Instead of the censer of error, they offered it before God. Blessed is your birth, which was worshiped.
Samekh — 28.
Myrrh worshiped you on its own behalf and on behalf of the spices, its relatives.

The detestable carved images were its companions, which its anointers used to anoint. [Through you the perfumes became fragrant, through the oil of Mary who anointed you.] Blessed is your fragrance, which made us fragrant.
Samekh — 29.

The gold that had been worshiped worshiped you when the Magi offered it. Having been worshiped in a cast image, it gave that worship to you. Together with its worshipers it worshiped you, acknowledging that you are

the one worthy of worship. Blessed is he who reclaimed his worship.
Ayin — 30.
The evil one and his forces fled—he who had reveled in the world. On the height they sacrificed a calf to him; in the gardens they slaughtered bulls

for him. [He swallowed all creation; destruction filled his belly.] Blessed is he who came and emptied him.
Ayin — 31.
Our Lord had said of him that he had fallen from heaven. His [?] was

abhorrent; he had fallen from his greatness. Mary's foot trampled him who had struck Eve with his heel. Blessed is he who brought him low by his birth.
Pe — 32.
The Chaldeans were wandering everywhere

and leading people astray. The heralds of error were in confusion throughout the world. They were silenced, defeated by the heralds of truth. Blessed is the birth that was proclaimed.
Pe — 33.
Sin had spread
its nets for the hunt. Thanks to your birth, which tore apart the nets of error! The soul that had been caught in the depths flew to the heights. Blessed is he

your birth persuaded us and gave us life. Blessed is he who devised a way to give us life.
Qoph — 35.
The complaints of the creatures that were worshiped were silently asking for freedom. The liberator of all heard, and, unable

to bear it, he descended. He clothed himself in the slave in the womb; he came out and freed creation. Blessed is he who traded for his creation.
Resh — 36.
Mercy welled up on high at the sound of the creatures crying out.
Gabriel was sent; he came and announced your conception. When you came to birth, the watchers announced your coming forth. Blessed by all is the worship of you. Resh. 37. For greater is the joy
of birth than of conception. Only one angel announced your conception to us, but companies of watchers announced the joy of your birth. Blessed is the good news of you on your day. Shin. 38.
I too will offer you praise on your day, O worshiped one. Accept the fruit I have, and give me the mercy you have. For if my wickedness has given what is mine, how much will you give,
you who are good! Blessed is your abundance in your works. Taw. 39. Both things I asked for came to us in your birth itself: you put on the visible body; may your hidden power

clothe us. Our body became your clothing; your Spirit became our robe. Blessed is he who adorned himself and adorned us. Taw. 40. The depths and the heights marveled that your birth subdued the rebels, for hostages
we gave you, and the Advocate you gave us. As hostages went up from us, the mighty one came down to us. Blessed is he who took and sent. Taw. 41. Come, all you mouths, be in harmony
and become like waters and wells of sound. May the Holy Spirit come and sing praise through it all to the Father, who saved us through his Son's birth. Blessed by all is he at his Son's birth.
Change of melody. Response: Glory to you in your entirety, from all. Glory to you in your entirety, from all.
Who indeed, being mortal, can speak about the one who gives life to all, who left the height of his greatness and descended to littleness? The one who makes all great, through his birth
has enlarged my weak understanding, so that I may speak about your birth—not to search out your greatness, but to proclaim your grace. Blessed is he who is hidden and revealed in the accounts of him.
It is a great wonder that the Son dwelt wholly within a body. He lived wholly in it, and it had room for him; he dwelt in it without being confined. His whole will was in it; his full
extent was not in it. Who can adequately describe how, while he dwelt wholly in the body, he also dwelt wholly in all creation? Blessed is the limitless one who became limited.
Your greatness is hidden from us; your grace is revealed before us. I will keep silent, my Lord, about your greatness and speak about your grace. Your grace clung to you
and bent you down toward our wickedness. Your grace made you an infant; your grace made you a human being. It contracted and expanded your greatness. Blessed is the power that became small and great.
Glory to him who became one below, though by nature he is the Most High. In his love he became Mary's firstborn, though he is the firstborn of the Godhead. In name he became a child

of Joseph, though he is the child of the Most High. By his will he became a human being, though by nature he is God. Glorious are your will and your nature. Blessed is your glory, which put on our image.
Your birth too, my Lord, became a mother to created things, for it labored and gave birth anew to humanity, which gave birth to you. Humanity gave birth to you bodily;

you gave birth to it spiritually. Your whole purpose in coming to birth was to give birth to humanity in your likeness. Your birth became the source of birth for all. Blessed is he who became a child and made everyone young.
Though human hope had been crushed, hope grew abundant at your birth. The heavenly beings announced good news of hope to humankind. Satan, who had cut off our hope, was cutting off his own hope
with his own hands when he saw that hope had increased. For those without hope, your birth became a spring gushing with hope. Blessed is the hope that brought good news.
The day of your birth resembles you, for it is desirable and beloved like you. Though we did not see your birth, we have loved it as though we were there at the time. On your day we see
you—that is, an infant like you. As it is loved by everyone, look, the churches rejoice in it. Your day has adorned and been adorned. Blessed is your day, which came into being for our sake.
Your day gave us a gift whose equal the Father has no more to give. He did not send us seraphim, nor did cherubim come down to us. The watchers, the suns, did not come.
But the Firstborn who is served—who can adequately give thanks that immeasurable greatness lay in a lowly manger? Blessed is he who gave us everything he possessed.

Your birth brought joy to that generation, and your day brings joy to ours. The blessedness of that generation was doubled, for they saw both your birth and your day. The blessedness of later generations was less, for the day of

your birth alone they see. Yet because those who were near you were divided, the blessedness of later generations became greater: although they had not seen you, they believed in you. Blessed is the blessedness you have added to us!
The Magi rejoiced from afar; the scribes proclaimed from nearby. The prophet made known his reading, and Herod his own savagery. The scribes presented interpretations; the Magi

presented offerings. It is a wonder that, because of one infant, the people of his own land rushed forward with their swords, and foreigners with their offerings. Blessed is your birth, which stirred everyone!
Mary’s lap amazed me: it was large enough for you, my Lord, and embraced you. All creation was too small to cover your greatness. Earth and heaven are too small to serve
as folds of a garment covering your divinity. The lap of the earth is too small for you, yet Mary’s lap is large enough for you. He dwelt in a lap and healed with the hem of his garment.
He wrapped himself in swaddling clothes in lowliness, and offerings were presented to him. He wore garments in his youth, and help flowed from them. He clothed himself in the waters of baptism,
and rays came forth from them. He wore linen cloths in death, and victories were revealed in them. His exaltations accompanied his humiliations. Blessed is he who joined his glory to his suffering!
All these changes of clothing the Merciful One took off and put on, devising a way to clothe Adam in the glory he had taken off. He wrapped himself in swaddling clothes alongside Adam’s leaves,

and wore garments in place of Adam’s skins. He was baptized because of Adam’s sin and embalmed because of Adam’s death. He rose and raised Adam in glory. Blessed is he who descended, clothed himself in Adam, and ascended!
Although your birth was sufficient for Adam’s children as for Adam—O Great One who became an infant, through your birth you brought me to birth anew! O Pure One who was baptized,

in your washing let us wash ourselves clean of filth! O Living One who was embalmed, let us gain life through your death! I will praise your whole being with the word “all.” Glory to your whole being from us all!

A variation, to the same tune.
Response: Glory to you from every mouth on this day of your birth!
Infants were killed because of your birth, O Giver of life to all. Yet the one being slain was a king—our Lord, the Lord of the kingdom. While that tyrant schemed, substitutes
were given to him, slain. Clothed in the mysteries of his slaying, they received heavenly ranks—these substitutes whom earthly people offered. Blessed is the King who exalted them!
All the kings of David’s house carried the throne and crown of David’s son and handed them on to one another, like guardians of things entrusted to them. [There was an end to priests, prophets

and kings.] In one they reached their limit and their boundary, for the Lord of everything came and took everything from them. He ended the lines of succession of everything. Blessed is he who clothed himself in what belonged to him!
The doves moaned in Bethlehem, for the serpent had destroyed their young. The eagle set out for Egypt, to go down and receive the promises. Egypt rejoiced in him, for she had [the means
to repay her debts. She had killed Joseph’s children;] she labored for Joseph’s son and repaid her debts for Joseph’s children. Blessed is he who called him out of Egypt!

The scribes read every day that a star would rise from Jacob. For the people there were a voice and a trumpet; for the nations, a shining and an explanation. They have the books, and we have the deeds;
they have the branches, and we have their fruits. The scribes read in books; the Magi see in deeds the radiance of that reading. Blessed is he who gave us their books as well!
Who is capable of speaking about the hidden and visible acts of the star of light that went before those carrying offerings? It appeared and proclaimed the crown;
it concealed itself and hid the body. It served the Son in two ways, as herald and guardian. It guarded his body and proclaimed his crown. Blessed is he who made his heralds wise!
The tyrant watched the Magi who asked, “Where is the king’s son?” Though his heart was gloomy, he questioned them cheerfully. He sent wolves with the sheep
to kill the Lamb of God. The Lamb was going to Egypt to judge them from there, he who had delivered them from there. Blessed is he who in turn brought them into subjection!
The Magi informed the tyrant, “Whenever your servants mingle with us, the star of light hides itself, and the paths are concealed.” The blessed men did not know
that evildoers were posing as worshipers. The bitter king sent them to destroy the sweet fruit, which bitter people ate and became sweet. Praise to you, medicine of life!
When the Magi received the command to go and search for him, it is written of them that they saw that star of light and rejoiced. Clearly it had hidden itself
and so they rejoiced at seeing it. It overthrew all the evildoers [?]; it rose and summoned the worshipers. It overthrew one side and summoned the other. Blessed is he who triumphed on both sides!
How did the unclean man who killed children neglect the Child? Justice restrained him, so that he expected the Magi to return to him. As he delayed, he set about hunting down the one worshiped
and his worshipers. His hands were left empty of everything: the offerings and the worshipers flew away from the tyrant to the king’s son. Glory to the one who knows every stratagem!
The clear-minded Magi reflected as they slept on their beds: sleep became a mirror, and a dream shone like light. The murderer
they saw, and they were terrified at his deceit: he was sharpening an already sharpened sword. A Watcher was teaching the sleepers. Blessed is he who made the innocent shrewd!
The innocent who believed came to know the two comings of Christ, but the foolish scribes did not perceive even one coming. The nations received life through one
and will be raised there at the last. The people whose understanding is blind were scattered by one coming; the second will erase their memory. Blessed is the King who came and is coming!
The Savior dawned upon the blind, but they were looking toward others. The Sun displayed his rays, but they were wrapped in darkness. The radiant one sent light
and brought the children of light to reveal to the children of darkness, “Look, the light is among you, but a covering lies over your eyes.” Glory to you, new Sun!
The prophets announced his birth but did not specify its time. He sent the Magi, and they came and made its time known.
But the Magi, who made the time known, did not specify which child. The triumphant star of light [?]. Blessed is he who was interpreted through them all!
They suppressed Isaiah’s trumpet, which sounded out about the pure conception. They silenced the harp of the Psalms, which sang about his priesthood. They silenced the lyre of the Spirit,
which also sang about his kingship. Beneath a great silence they confined the great birth that made those above and those below cry out together. Blessed is he who dawned from within the silence!

His voice became a hidden key and opened the mouths of the Magi. Because the heralds in Judea had fallen silent, they sounded their voice throughout creation. And the good news that those people had suppressed,

people from far away carried and brought with them. Those who had suppressed it began to hear their own words from foreigners as they cried out about the Son of David. Blessed is he who silenced them with our voice!
Because the people withheld offerings and did not present them to the king’s son, his messenger went out to the nations and brought them with their offerings. Yet he did not bring them all.
For it could not hold them. The little bosom of Bethlehem, which is the bosom of the holy Church, grew wide and embraced her children. Blessed is he who made the barren woman fruitful!
In Bethlehem the murderers harvested tender blossoms, so that among them the tender seed might perish, in which the living bread lay hidden. The ear of life had fled,

so that it might come into the reaper’s hand at harvest. The cluster that fled while still an infant gave itself to the winepress, so that souls might shine through its wine. Glory to you, treasure of life!
The evildoers entered the paradise filled with fruit—infants. They shook blossoms from the branches and destroyed young grapes and shoots. Pure offerings
the troublemaker offered without knowing it: woe to him, but blessedness to them! Bethlehem yielded her firstfruits and gave virgin fruits to the Holy One. Blessed is he who received the firstfruits!
When the scribes fell silent through envy, and the Pharisees through jealousy, people of stone cried out and gave praise. Those who possessed hearts of stone sang praises before the stone

that was rejected and became the chief stone. Stones grew tender through the Stone and acquired speaking mouths. The stones cried out through the Stone’s power. Blessed is your birth, which made the stones cry out!
The distant nations saw the star written of in Scripture, to put the people nearby to shame. Oh, the people who teach and boast, yet turned to learn from a people how

and where they had seen it—that rising light of which Balaam spoke! A foreigner was the one who announced it, and foreigners were the ones who saw it. Blessed is he who stirred his own people to jealousy!

May my petition approach your door, and my need your treasury. Give to me, my Lord, without reckoning, as God gives to a human being. For if you have given abundantly, it is as the Son of the Good One;

and if you give still more, it is as the Son of the King. If I have done wrong, it is as one made of dust, like Adam, an offspring of Adam. And you are good, and the Son of the Good One. Glory to you who resemble your Father!
The people who hold the Scriptures do not perceive that these proclaim their offenses. They cry out about their departure and tell of our entrance. Look, the fool reads in his books
the promises allotted to us! While boasting of his Scriptures, he reads us his own indictment and bears witness to our inheritance. Blessed is he who made them labor for our rest!
A pair of heralds spread abroad the qualities of the Only-Begotten: the star of light and John, one a radiance and the other a voice. For the one they proclaimed
was both Word and Light. A voice and a ray served him: the radiance proclaimed his light, and the voice his wisdom. Blessed is the Firstborn on the lips of his heralds!
John looked at him and cried out, “This is the Lamb of God!” The Lamb had grown strong and matured, and came to be an offering. John was not afraid
when he cried out, “Look, this is he!” For even if the murderers advanced, the time for sprinkling had come, so that through his blood there might be forgiveness. Blessed is he who pays our debts!
The glorious star of light was not like John. For sometimes it shone and made the road straight for the simple, but sometimes it set

and hid the path from the wolves. It kept the Lamb from slaughter so that on his appointed day he might come to the slaughter through which the flock would receive atonement. Blessed is he who redeemed his possessions through him!
Change of tune. To the tune: “Blessed are you, Ephrathah.” Response: Glory to him who sent him! Glory to him who sent him!
Blessed are you, Church, for within you thunders the great feast, the festival of the King! Abandoned Zion—her gates are very thirsty and lie desolate, deprived of festivals.

Blessed are your gates, which were opened but could not contain them, and your courts, which were enlarged but could not hold them! Within you the nations thunder: they have cried out and silenced that people.
Blessed are you, Church, for at your festivals the watchers rejoice among your celebrations. For on one night the watchers sang praise on earth, which had concealed and withheld praise.
Blessed are your voices, which were sown and harvested and gathered into storehouses in heaven. Your mouth is a censer, and your voices are like incense, spreading fragrance at your festivals.
Blessed are you, Church, for all offerings come to you at this feast. Once the Magi, among deceitful people, presented their offerings to the Truth.
Blessed is your dwelling, into which the King's Son stooped and settled, receiving worship with gifts. The gold of the West and the silks of the East are offered at your festivals.
Blessed are you, Church, for the tyrant king who slaughters infants is not among you. For he killed the children in Bethlehem in a frenzy, to put to death the Child who gives life to everyone.
Blessed are your children, who were envied and worshiped by kings who [?] in worshiping you. May the crown of the East, which trampled those who love you, be trampled by your beloved ones.
Blessed are you, Church, for Isaiah too rejoices in you through his prophecy: “Look,” he says, “the virgin will conceive and bear a child whose name is a great mystery.” Oh,
the interpretation revealed in the Church! Two names were blended and became one: Emmanuel—God is with you at all times, for he has joined you to his members.
Blessed are you, Church, through Micah, who cried out that a shepherd would come from Ephrathah. For he came to Bethlehem to take from her the stock of Jesse and shepherd the nations.
Blessed are your sheep, which have been marked with his mark, and your ewes, which have been guarded by his word. You, you are the Church, the enduring Bethlehem, for within you is the bread of life.
Blessed are you, Church, for Daniel too, the man greatly beloved, rejoices in you. He declared that the glorious Messiah would be killed and that the holy city would be destroyed through his killing.

Woe to the people who were cast away and did not return! Blessed are the nations who were called and did not turn back! The invited guests excused themselves, and others in their place enjoy their wedding feasts.

Blessed are you, Church, for King David now sings of you with his lyre. Through the Spirit he sang concerning him: “You are my Son, and in the splendors of holiness I have begotten you today.” Blessed
are your ears, which have been cleansed to hear. Awaken to his day as his body, and proclaim it. In Zion the festival was afflicted, and she grew sorrowful. Gladden him who has gladdened you.
Blessed are you, Church, for all the festivals flew from Zion and settled with you. Within you the weary prophets found rest from that toil and dishonor in Judah.

Blessed are her books, which have been spread open in your temples, and her festivals, which have been celebrated joyfully in your sanctuaries. Zion is desolate, while today the worlds thunder at your festivals.
Blessed are you, Church, with the ten beatitudes that our Lord gave as a complete mystery. For all numbers depend on ten; therefore ten beatitudes have made you complete.
Blessed are your crowns, which have been woven from all the holy blessings blended into every crown. Blessed one, crowned with every blessing, cast a blessing on me too.
Blessed are you, Ephrathah, mother of kings, for from you dawned the Lord of crowns. Micah announced to you that he is from eternity and that the span of his times cannot be comprehended. Blessed
are your eyes, which welcomed him before everyone else. He made you worthy to see him when he dawned. You received the first blessing and the beginning of joys before everyone else.
Blessed are you, Bethlehem, for fortified towns and mighty cities were jealous of you. As they were jealous of you, so women and virgins, the daughters of rulers, were jealous of Mary.

Blessed is the young woman whom he made worthy to be his lodging, and also the village that he made worthy to be his dwelling. He chose for himself a poor young woman and a small village, so that he might humble himself.
Blessed are you, Bethlehem, for in you a beginning came to the Son who has been in the Father from eternity. It is hard to comprehend how he who is before all ages subjected

himself to time in you. Blessed are your ears, for the Lamb of God first bleated in you and leaped for joy in you. He was little in your manger, yet became known in every region and was worshiped by all creatures.
Blessed are you too, Mary, for your name is great and exalted because of your child. Can you indeed say how, and to what extent, and where the Great One who became little dwelt within you?

Blessed is your mouth, which gave thanks and did not venture further, and your tongue, which praised and did not investigate. His mother marveled at him even while carrying him. Who could comprehend him?
O woman whom no man has known, how can we behold the Son you bore? For the eye cannot take in the changing forms of glory
upon him. For tongues of fire dwell in him who sent tongues at his ascension. Let every tongue beware, for our investigation is a debt, and our inquiry is fire.
Blessed is the priest who, in the sanctuary, offered to the Father the Father's child, the fruit plucked from [?], though he belongs wholly to the divine majesty. Blessed

are his hands, which were sanctified by offering him, and his gray hairs, which labored to embrace him. The Spirit in the temple longed for his entry, and when he was crucified, she tore it and went out.
That chief of the angels gave you a greeting of peace as a pledge of holiness. Earth became a new heaven for him, for the angels descended and sang praises
in it. The inhabitants of heaven surrounded your dwelling because of the King's Son who dwelt in you. Your dwelling below resembled heaven above in its watchfulness.
Change of melody. Refrain: Blessed is your birth, which gladdens all creatures.
The first year of our Savior's birth is the beginning of good things and the foundation of life. For it bears an abundance of victories and the sum of all help,
like the first day in the beginning, the great pillar of created things. It bears the structure of creation, and the firstborn day bears help for humanity.
The year, the second year of our Savior's birth: in it the Magi rejoice, and in it the Pharisees mourn; in it treasures are opened, and in it kings are alarmed; and in it infants
are slaughtered. For in it offerings both lovely and terrible were offered in Bethlehem. Love offered gold, and envy offered children by the sword.
The day of the one who enlightens all rejoices in his birth. It is a pillar of rays that drove away with its beams the deeds of darkness, after the pattern of that day on which
light was created and split apart the darkness spread over the beauty of created things. The ray of our Savior's birth entered and split apart the darkness over the heart.
The first day, the head and beginning, is a symbol of the root that made everything sprout. The day of our Savior, planted within the world, is far more glorious than it. His death
is like a root within the earth, and his resurrection like a treetop in heaven. His words reach every region like his branches, and his fruit, his body, is for those who eat it.

On the second day let us praise, at his birth, the Son, the second, and the voice of the First. He commanded, and the firmament came into being; he separated the waters above and gathered the seas below.
He who separated the waters from the waters [?] parted from the angels and descended to humanity. In place of the waters that he commanded to gather, he opened a spring of life and gave drink.
On the third day let us weave a crown of psalms with hymns and offer it with one voice to the birth of him who made blossoms and flowers spring up on the day
Third. Now he himself, who makes everything grow, came down and became a holy flower. From thirsty ground he sprang up and rose, to adorn and crown the innocent.
Fourth day. One in four, let us give thanks for the birth of him who created, on the fourth day, the pair of lights that fools worshiped, and became blind
and lost their sight. The Lord of the lights came down, and like the sun he shone upon us from the womb. His rays opened the eyes of the blind; his beams enlightened those who had gone astray.
Fifth day. Let us praise him who created, on the fifth day, creeping creatures and sea monsters. From their kind came the crafty serpent, who led our mother astray, a foolish girl without
understanding. The deceiver who had mocked the girl was exposed by the dove. From an innocent womb [the wise one dawned and came forth], who crushed the crafty one.
Sixth day. Let us praise him who created Adam on Friday. The Evil One envied him; like a friend, he cunningly cheered him and offered him poison
in food. The medicine of life was shared out to them both. He put on a body and approached them both. The mortal tasted him and lived through him; the devourer who ate him was emptied.

Seventh day. Let us hallow the Holy One, who hallowed the Sabbath to give rest to the animals. The Good One, who does not grow weary, cared for humanity and cared for the animals. Because freedom had fallen
under the yoke, he came to birth and submitted to slavery in order to set it free. He received a slap [from his servant] in the court. As Lord, he broke the yoke laid upon the free.
Eighth day, which circumcised the Hebrews. Let us give thanks to him who commanded his namesake Joshua to circumcise with flint the people whose bodies were circumcised but whose hearts were pagan
within. See, on the eighth day, he who circumcises everyone came like an infant to be circumcised. Though Abraham’s sign was upon his flesh, the blind daughter of Zion reviled him.
Tenth day. Let us offer praise through its number, for yod, the letter of the glorious name Jesus, is ten in numerical value. Like a lord, this number turns the numbers back.
For when counting reaches ten, it turns back again to begin from one. Oh, the great mystery in Jesus, whose power turns created things back!
The Firstborn, who purifies everyone, on the day of his purification purified the purification of the firstborn and was presented as an offering. The Lord of the offering had to present offerings
of a bird. At his birth the types were fulfilled; at his purification and circumcision, wonders. He came and paid the debts in his descent; at his resurrection he ascended and sent treasures.
Change of tune. Response: Praise to you, Son of the Lord of all. Repeat.

Light became a herald for the shining one whom Mary bore. For his conception took place when light was victorious, and his birth likewise took place when the sun was victorious. Blessed is the victorious one!
Yod is placed at the beginning of your name; it is placed at ten in the month of Nisan. On the tenth you entered the womb. Your conception bears the mystery of the number of perfection.
The number ten is complete. [On the tenth of Nisan you entered the womb. The number six is also perfect. On the sixth of January your birth gladdened the six directions.
The number ten is a limit.] And the sixth is the limit of limits. On the tenth was his conception; on the sixth, his birth. His birth gladdened the four quarters [and the heights and depths].
The name of Joseph was not sufficient for him to be your father, for it was weak. Your name gave him the letter yod. Your name strengthened Joseph’s name so that he could be your father.

Christ, too, in his mercy gave the first of his letters to Mary’s name. See, their names depend upon his names; through his power their bodies, too, depended upon him, together with all created things.
For Mary, who bore Christ in her womb and on her lap, bore the beginning of his name, the first letter of the name “Christ,” just as his power bears her body.
For Mary could not have borne his body without his power. He showed what is hidden through what is visible: not even their names could have existed without him.
He gave his initial letters to his forefathers, who were his ancestors. Just as their bodies shone through him, so he also adorned their names with his names.
Nor, again, did John himself baptize his body without his power. Yodh bore the name of John, just as the power of Jesus bore John himself.
If he lent the beauty of his letters to their names, if he mingled his majestic beauty with their names, how much more, then, did he mingle his hidden power with their names!
And just as numbering has only ten ranks, creation has six sides: height and depth, and the four directions, which are filled with you.
Yodh, the letter of Jesus our King, is the queen of all numbers. Calculations depend on its completeness, just as all thoughts are mingled in Jesus.
The one greater than all descended in his entirety to an indescribable lowliness. He returned again from that lowliness and occupied the limitless height at the right hand.
It is a great wonder that he did not descend from that height gradually, little by little, to come into lowliness. He flew from the bosom of divinity to humanity.

For the sun, that sun of yours, proclaims your mystery as though with a mouth. In winter it descends to the depths as a symbol of you; in summer it rises to the heights in your likeness and reigns over all.

The symbol of your conception, and that of John your herald, has also become great to me [?]. The mystery of your conceptions and your births is portrayed in light and darkness and is clear to anyone who understands.
John’s conception took place in Tishrin, when darkness advances. Your own conception took place in Nisan, when light reigns over darkness and subdues it.

I give thanks for your first birth, which is concealed and hidden from all creatures. Again I give thanks for your second birth, which is revealed and younger than all the creatures that came into being through your hands.
The Only-Begotten has two births: one above and one below, one foreign and unfamiliar to all, and one belonging to our race. Both astonish the whole human race.
The day of your birth, too, fittingly falls in Kanun as a symbol: in it light takes back from darkness the hours it swallowed, just as you took us back from the one who swallowed us.
Nisan portrays your conception, crying out, “Look, the light is enclosed in the womb!” In Kanun the pair of lights came forth: you from the womb, and the sun with you from within the darkness.
To the same tune.
The honored shelter in [?]—if the animals in it remained chaste, how could Mary, in whom Emmanuel dwelt, turn to sexual union?
Your own will exalted you and sanctified you; your Lord also added to this and adorned you. Noah’s animals were restrained by compulsion, but you by your own will. Response:

Praises to his birth!
Stanza 2 = XXV, 17.
3. It is not that intercourse is defiling, nor that marriage is unclean. The wings of chastity are greater and lighter
than marriage. Intercourse, though pure, is timid; in its modesty it takes refuge in darkness. All confidence belongs to chastity, which is clothed

in light.
4. The light of peace was in your dwellings and gave no place to sexual union, for there were no secret deeds within your camp.
You are full of glory. The shadows of weakness and desire vanished in the Savior’s rays. You became entirely spiritual, of the Spirit, because you gave birth to the spiritual one.

If we say, “She is a virgin,” her pregnancy rebukes us; and if we say, “A man’s wife,” her virginity cries out. If we say, “She is both a virgin and a man’s wife,” she is one body, and it does not allow
us. It was a wonder and a marvel to the upright; it was distress and torment to the scribes. Her virginity was hidden, and her breasts were full. Praise to him for everything!
Conception in the world is set in motion by bodily desire, which is in the limbs. Your pure conception wiped away and removed the desire for arousal from your limbs.
He poured holiness and purity into you and filled you; he washed you with holy streams, so that whoever sees you might say, “How blessed is this woman who is praised!”
The glorious one whom she conceived had imprinted himself upon your mind as with a seal. And even when he had been born, he was, so to speak, in you, for all of him was peering out from
your limbs. His radiance was spread over your beauty, and her love was anointed over your whole being. You wove a garment for him, but he spread his glory over all your senses.
How greatly Error went astray! She gathered bitterness from sweet flowers, like the [?] that eats sweet fruits, which turn within it into deadly gall.
Error, too, gathers deadly poison for her lovers from sweet writings. The serpent’s children offer a cup in which they have mixed the dragon’s gall.
Blessed are you, Church, the bee that has so many sweet blossoms! You have one Nisan, the Egyptian one, and a second Nisan, the Hebrew one. From
holy flowers she gathers; from them all she collects every benefit. Blessed are you, Church, for you have gathered sweetness from the blossoms of your sanctuary!
The bee portrayed your likeness: she left the blossoms in her own land and flew no short distance, for the scent had reached her of the sweet flower that sprang up in Judah.
She came and gathered sweetness with her ears, took hold of it, and carried it away. But Jerusalem poured out the sweetness, and the nations ran and gathered it.
